items.title: [難過] 媽媽要我繳家裡房貸
items.human_voice:
我們家本來一直都是租房子。我大學剛畢業那年，媽媽出了頭期款買了一間房，並登記在我名下，但媽媽是預告登記人。我剛出社會薪水有限，每個月只能給媽媽5000到一萬幫忙貼補貸款。

結果才過兩三年，媽媽最近突然說她沒辦法繳了，要我馬上把整筆房貸扛起來。我知道她一開始買房，只是怕自己老了沒地方住，並不是單純要買給我。現在她繳不起、不想繳了，就要求我犧牲我自己的生涯規劃，立刻開始負擔每月 25,000 元、長達 30 年的房貸直到老死...

因為本身有轉職進修的規劃（當然生活費學費都自己負擔），現在媽媽甚至威脅我：如果我還敢堅持要唸書而不是直接找個工作上班，她就要把房子賣掉，叫我滾出去租房子。

我不知道她到底是不是認真的，但心裡有時候甚至覺得，也許真的賣掉也好？等我日後職涯穩定了，再考慮買房給她住也不遲。

【想請教大家的問題】

1. 我應該放棄考試進修的計畫嗎？
沒有特別專長的我，如果現在妥協，也只能去找一般的行政職，然後每個月硬扛 25,000 的房貸扛到老死，大家覺得為了維持這間房子，這樣犧牲一輩子的職涯發展值得嗎？

2. 面對媽媽威脅賣房，大家會怎麼選？
大家會建議順水推舟讓她賣掉（或搬出去自己租屋切割），把存款留給自己翻身？還是應該妥協？

3. 既然我媽堅持要我趕快扛，還是我現在申請寬限期，讀書期間扛起利息，讀完書再扛房貸，缺點是這樣房貸額會變高。

心情真的很茫然，希望能聽聽大家的過來人經驗或客觀分析，謝謝大家！

--
Sent from nPTT on my iPhone 15

items.title: How to accurately calculate road distance from GPS traces with GPS gaps and map matching?
items.human_voice:
I am developing a taxi/ride-hailing application where I need to calculate the actual road distance traveled by a driver as accurately as possible.

My current approach is:

When a trip starts, I collect the driver's GPS location every 5 seconds.

I store the GPS points in Redis until the trip ends.

I apply a Kalman filter to remove noisy or invalid GPS points.

I use Valhalla for map matching.

If Valhalla fails, I fall back to OSRM, then Google Maps.

If all map-matching services fail, I calculate the distance using the filtered GPS coordinates.

With this approach, I currently get around 85% accuracy for the total trip distance.

The problem
I need to achieve 99%+ accuracy, because the calculated distance is used for taxi trip/fare calculation.

The main issues are:

GPS points can be inaccurate or noisy.

GPS gaps can occur between consecutive points.

GPS can completely disappear for a period of time.

Drivers may travel through tunnels or areas with poor GPS coverage.

GPS coordinates can suddenly jump to an incorrect location.

Map matching can fail for some sections.

Valhalla, OSRM, and Google Maps can return different distances.

My questions
Is there a more advanced approach for calculating road distance from GPS trajectories?

Specifically, what is the recommended way to:

Handle GPS gaps and GPS outages?

Reconstruct missing sections of a trip?

Improve GPS filtering beyond a standard Kalman filter?

Use HMM, Particle Filters, Sensor Fusion, or other map-matching techniques?

Handle cases where map matching fails?

Decide between different routing/map-matching results?

Perform map matching continuously during the trip versus processing the entire trip afterward?

I would also like to understand how production ride-hailing systems such as Uber, Ola, and Rapido generally approach this problem.

Is 99%+ road-distance accuracy realistically achievable using GPS alone, or are additional signals such as speed, heading, accelerometer, gyroscope, or road-network data normally required?

I am looking for a production-grade architecture/algorithm, rather than a simple Haversine-distance calculation.

¿Cómo crear un usuario y su carpeta personal (/home) simultáneamente en Linux usando useradd?
items.human_voice:
Necesitaba crear un usuario nuevo en Linux (Kali) y asegurar que su directorio /home se generara al mismo tiempo.

Lo que probé y aprendí:

Inicialmente intenté usar comandos directos, pero descubrí que existen dos formas efectivas de lograrlo desde la terminal:

Uso estándar: sudo useradd -m nombre_usuario (la opción -m genera la carpeta personal de forma automática).

Ruta explícita: sudo useradd -md /home/nombre_usuario nombre_usuario (para definir la ruta del directorio explícitamente).

Además, comprobé que para verificar la creación correcta se utilizan los comandos ls /home, id nombre_usuario y grep nombre_usuario /etc/passwd.

items.title: Como estruturar automação de carregamento dinâmico de dados em ListBox no VBA de forma escalável?
items.human_voice:
Estou desenvolvendo uma aplicação em Excel com VBA que precisa carregar dados de múltiplas colunas em uma ListBox.
Já conheço soluções que usam loops (Do While, For Each) e também a atribuição direta de intervalos (ListBox.List = Range(...).Value).

No entanto, meu objetivo é algo mais escalável e automatizado:

Detectar dinamicamente o intervalo de dados (sem precisar definir manualmente).

Suportar múltiplas colunas e diferentes tamanhos de planilha.

Evitar duplicação de código e manter performance em planilhas grandes.

Exemplo simplificado do que já tentei:

vba
Listagem.Clear
Listagem.List = Sheets("Lista").Range("A1:C10").Value
Funciona, mas exige definir o intervalo manualmente.

Pergunta: Qual seria a melhor prática para estruturar essa automação em VBA, garantindo escalabilidade e manutenção em cenários mais complexos (ex.: milhares de linhas, múltiplas colunas variáveis)?

items.title: Doom Emacs で tab-width の値を変更しても意図した通りに動作しない
items.human_voice:
質問内容
VSCodeのようにタブキーを押すとスペース４つ分入力してほしいですが

画像のように一回目の入力では２で二回目は6入力されてしまいます。

何が影響しているのでしょうか？

実現しようとしていること
VSCodeのようにタブキーでスペース４分入力　その次は4入力して4,4と追記する形。

{などで改行したときもインデントを揃えてその{からさらに１タブ分入力する形。

現状
一回目の入力では２で二回目は6入力されてしまいます。

config.elでは実験のため８にしています。

フォントは規定に戻すためにコメントアウト。

確認したこと
M-x describe variable より tab-width lu 8

M-x evil-expression より (setq tab-width 4)で実行しました結果が同じです。2_now()の2のところまでカーソルが進みます。

config.el
;; =============================================================================
;; LSP 自動起動
;; =============================================================================
(after! lsp-mode
(setq lsp-auto-guess-root t
lsp-auto-configure t
lsp-enable-on-save t
lsp-keep-workspace-alive t))

;; 特定のメジャーモード時に自動起動
(add-hook 'python-mode-hook #'lsp) ;; Python
(add-hook 'typescript-mode-hook #'lsp) ;; TypeScript
(add-hook 'js-mode-hook #'lsp) ;; JavaScript
(add-hook 'go-mode-hook #'lsp) ;; Go
(add-hook 'rust-mode-hook #'lsp) ;; Rust
(add-hook 'c++-mode-hook #'lsp) ;; C++
(add-hook 'c-mode-hook #'lsp) ;; C

;; =============================================================================
;; 自動整形
;; =============================================================================
;; 自動整形を無効化
;;(setq-default electric-indent-mode nil)

;; LSP の自動フォーマットを無効化
(after! lsp-mode
(setq lsp-enable-on-type-formatting nil))

;; prettier などのフォーマッターを無効化
(after! format
(setq +format-on-save-enabled-modes nil))

;; =============================================================================
;; Theme
;; =============================================================================
(setq doom-theme 'tokyo-night)

;; Use fonts
;; (setq doom-font (font-spec :family "SauceCodePro NF" :size 22)
;; doom-variable-pitch-font (font-spec :family "SauceCodePro NF" :size 22)
;; doom-big-font (font-spec :family "SauceCodePro NF" :size 23)) ; プレゼンモード用

(setq doom-font nil)

;; True color
(setq xterm-color-preserve-properties t)

;; =============================================================================
;; Hover
;; =============================================================================

(after! lsp-ui
;; ドキュメント表示の設定
(setq lsp-ui-doc-enable t
lsp-ui-doc-position 'at-point ;; カーソル位置に表示
))

(after! evil
(map! :map evil-normal-state-map
"K" #'lsp-ui-doc-glance))

;; ~/.doom.d/config.el
(use-package! highlight-thing
:hook (prog-mode . highlight-thing-mode) ; プログラミングモード全般で有効化
:config
(setq highlight-thing-delay-seconds 0.0)) ; ハイライトまでの遅延時間（秒）

;; nvim tokyo night theme
(custom-set-faces!
'(highlight-thing
:background "#3e4451" ; やや明るいダークグレー (例: One Darkの参照色)
:foreground nil ; 文字色は元のコードの色を維持 (指定したい場合は "#ffffff" 等)
)) ; 太字にする場合 (不要なら削除)

;; =============================================================================
;; Tabサイズ
;; =============================================================================

(setq-default prettier-enabled-modes nil)

(add-hook 'after-change-major-mode-hook
(lambda ()
(setq-local tab-width 8
indent-tabs-mode nil
evil-shift-width 8)))
;; 最初に実行される hook を使用
(setq-default tab-width 8
indent-tabs-mode nil
evil-shift-width 8)

;; ファイルを開いた直後に実行
(add-hook 'find-file-hook
(lambda ()
(setq-local tab-width 8
indent-tabs-mode nil
evil-shift-width 8)))

;; モード切り替え時
(add-hook 'after-change-major-mode-hook
(lambda ()
(setq-local tab-width 8
indent-tabs-mode nil
evil-shift-width 8)))

;; Prettier を無効化
(after! prettier
(prettier-mode -1)

Change journal policy to allow LLM use without disclosing it: A lot of people would not like that and it would make journal papers useless for hiring decisions.

items.title: How do I add to a conversation, without people getting defensive "that's not what I mean"?

Person A says something.
I respond, adding something to the conversation.
Person A gets defensive: "I didn't say that" or "that's not what I mean".

The context is: (1) a Redditor claimed to "pass the HSK4", a Chinese-language exam; (2) another Redditor said they shouldn't claim they passed the HSK4 when they only did a self-adminstered HSK4 exam (a fair point); (3) I replied

and added a concrete example which highlights why passing a mock exam is not essentially the same as passing an actual exam, linking to an example of a student who claimed to get 30 fewer marks on the actual exam. And I got this reply:

my critique was never that the mock papers differ much from real exam paper

But I didn't claim that Redditor said this---I'm adding to the conversation. The Redditor completely ignored what I said, and doubled-down on their claims. I wanted to participate in the conversation too, but it seems adding new information is unwelcome.

Another example was with with my landlord, who was saying I shouldn't use 5 electricity-heavy appliances simultaneously. I responded by saying I care about the environment and avoid using them regardless. But she replied by saying I can use them, and repeating back: not five at a time. I feel like I made a faux pas by expanding the topic beyond the original "5 electricity-heavy appliances" topic.

Similar situations have arose in totally different contexts (both online and offline; some I've forgotten, some are too lengthy to communicate), where I face the same problem: if I add to the conversation, people become unhappy with me.

items.title: How do I earn respect without constantly smiling?

I've realized I'm the only one who smiles near-constantly like this; whenever I am not smiling (when I'm focused on a task at my desk or walking down the hallway) my coworkers will ask me throughout the day if I'm doing alright, at which point I've noticed the only thing that reassures them isn't my words but my smile.

How can I let others (non-verbally) know that, despite not having a smile on my face, I am approachable, friendly and willing to listen and not trying to be disrespectful or dismissive?

items.title: Why human syntax breaks LLMs (and how to fix agentic coding)
items.human_voice:
Full technical essay with benchmarks & AST breakdowns:
https://aslang.dev/blog/why-llms-struggle-with-python-and-rustOver the past two years, watching coding agents generate code, we kept noticing an identical failure pattern: models spend 32% to 41% of their inference compute trapped in syntax repair loops.When we investigated the information theory behind this, we realized the problem is not model scale—it is the computational geometry of transformer attention heads when confronted with human-centric grammars:
1. Python's off-side rule: Lexing requires an internal LIFO indentation stack. Closing 3 blocks emits 0 characters. A single whitespace token split silently re-parents AST subtrees.
2. Rust's borrow checker: Validity depends on non-local constraint solving across lifetimes and CFGs. Autoregressive generation is strictly forward causal (O(1) feedforward); it cannot backpropagate lifetime conflicts backward during generation.We built AgentScript (ASL): an open-source, statically typed language using single-pass S-expressions that compiles directly to native Rust, Go, TypeScript, and WebAssembly (wasm32-wasip1).Key properties enforced by construction:
* Balanced parentheses by grammar: Left-to-right attention heads always know parent scope.
* Closed vocabulary (prelude.json): 100% of builtins are type-checked and evaluated; no unmodeled foreign calls.
* Sub-millisecond Wasm sandboxing: In-memory WASI preview1 execution in 0.038ms without Docker/microVM spin-up.
* Syntax repair collapse: Models spend 46.5% of generated tokens fixing syntax in Rust (our hard baseline) and 34.2% in Python. In AgentScript, repair iterations drop by 98.3% vs Rust baseline (from 4.8 cycles to 0.08), cutting syntax repair waste to just 1.2%.Our Mission: The Best Harness for Local Development with Small Models
While frontier models on cloud clusters partially brute-force messy human grammars, our mission is to build the most effective autonomous harness for local development with small models (SLMs: 3B to 31B like Qwen, Gemma, Llama) running directly on developer machines.On Apple Silicon or laptops, memory and attention are precious. A single-pass, parenthesis-balanced language combined with resident AST batch RPC eliminates the syntax churn and context rot that derail small models.Pre-Release Alpha & Active Development:
AgentScript is in early pre-release alpha—we do not have a tagged v0.1 release yet and are actively migrating to a 100% self-hosted compiler & WASI runtime. But even at this stage, empirical results inside agent loops are remarkably compelling.Try It Locally & In Your Agent Skills:
We do not offer an in-browser playground—test the real thing directly in realistic agent workflows:
1. CLI toolchain: curl -fsSL https://aslang.dev/install.sh | bash (or clone GenSEAM/asl & cargo build --release)
2. Equip agent skills (Claude Code, Cursor, Antigravity) with AST verification and batch RPC:
asl rpc '(:batch (:out "src/main.asl") (:sym "my_func"))'Terminal-Bench 4.0 Baseline (Macro Results, Not Cherry-Picked):
We packaged our baseline submission on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (tested on Gemma 4 31B under strict airgap boundaries):
* Macro Pass Rate: 13.5% across all 89 evaluated tasks (12 verified passes / 89 total tasks).
* Baseline Comparison: Common harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, CLI loops) score 0.0% on this suite when paired with open-weights models due to subshell state loss, quoting drift, and context blowup. Pure ASL achieves 13.5% on Gemma 31B in airgap.
* Token Economy: 77.3% token savings vs standard agent CLI baselines.Transcripts & submission tarball: https://github.com/GenSEAM/harness
Core compiler & runtime repo: https://github.com/GenSEAM/aslWe would love critical feedback from compiler engineers, language designers, and systems builders on the grammar design and agent steering architecture!

items.title: [心情] 她只說了一聲「喔」
items.human_voice:
2018年盛夏，藏壽司剛來台中開分店的時候，我約了她一同嘗鮮。

那是再普通不過的晚餐行程，通常她會跟我分享工作點滴，或許因為有著相似的背景，對
於她的故事頗有共鳴，但那天，我有點心不在焉。

距離我出發前往中國只剩不到一個月了，心中的焦慮與迷惘，壓過了拜訪新餐廳的期待，
況且，我還沒跟她說我的下一步，還沒跟她說我即將離開台中。

食量不大的她，只簡單吃了幾盤壽司；阮囊羞澀的我，仍計算著如何在有限預算內獲得最
大飽足感。

相較於她最愛的鼎泰豐，藏壽司明顯不是久坐久聊的地方，晚餐時光轉瞬即逝，結帳買單
，回家休息，準備迎接新的工作日。

我終於找到時機開了口：「7月開始我就不在台中了，因為有一個難得的機會，我要去中
國當英文老師。」

「喔，」這是她的唯一回應，沒有追問其他細節，於是我雲淡風輕地轉移話題。

回家以後，我一直在想，我到底在期待她有什麼反應？是不是哪怕一句「你幹嘛去？」都
能讓我義無反顧地回頭？雖然這聲「喔」非常符合她的典型反應，但我是不是想透過這個
職涯變換來測試，我在她心中的份量？

我沒有答案。

儘管我們不定期見面，豢養了內心對她的情愫，我也樂在其中，但這麼多年來她始終沒有
接受我，我在堅持什麼？為什麼不改變？

這個答案卻是清楚的，中國行沒有取消的可能。

6月底，我將滿滿家當裝進31吋的行李箱，買了一張單程機票，獨自一人來到桃園機場，
登上中國南方航空的班機，歸期未定，前途未卜。我和她的人生在台中短暫交集後，再度
走上了分岔路。

飛機起飛的那一刻，我閉上眼，決定暫時忘了她，那是我們相識的第17年。

--

items.title: ¿Qué patrón Regex necesito para encontrar ciertas palabras?
items.human_voice:
Estoy tratando de encontrar, en una lista, todas las palabras que cumplan con lo siguiente:

Las palabras encontradas, si busco "manzano", pueden contener:

Máximo 2 letras "a" o ninguna

Máximo 1 letra "m" o ninguna

Máximo 2 letras "n" o ninguna

Máximo 1 letra "o" o ninguna

Máximo 1 letra "z" o ninguna

Pero si busco con otra palabra diferente la cosa cambia.

Algunas palabras válidas, si buscase "manzano", serían:
manzano, mano, nam, azam, amanzon, monanza o aamnnoz

Porque las letras contenidas, existen en la palabra que se ha de buscar y porque las letras repetidas no se repiten más de lo que se repiten en esa misma palabra que se ha de buscar

Algunas palabras inválidas, si buscase "manzano", serían:
anana, zaza, ozono, etc.

Porque contienen más letras repetidas que las que existen en la palabra que busco, "manzano"

De momento, con la siguiente expresión regular, es con lo que estoy trabajando. Pero, en los resultados de las búsquedas, se pueden encontrar palabras que contienen letras con más repeticiones que las de la propia palabra a buscar.

^([manzano]){3,7}\r$

La palabras se buscan desde un TextBox. Puede cambiar. Así que la expresión regular anterior sería:
"^(["& TextBoxPalabra.text & "]){" & TextBoxMinimoDeLetras.text & "," & TextBoxMaximoDeLetras.text & "}\r$"

Lo siguiente es un ejemplo de lo que estoy usando para intentar conseguir lo que necesito:

' Clase eficiente para almacenar temporalmente y manipular cadenas.
ReadOnly stbl As New StringBuilder

' Lista donde se almacenan temporalmente datos.
ReadOnly lst1 As New List(Of String)

' Lista donde se almacenan temporalmente datos sin líneas repetidas.
ReadOnly hset As New HashSet(Of String)

ReadOnly strg As String
WithEvents TextBox1 As New TextBox

Private Sub Button1_Click(sender As Object, e As EventArgs) Handles Button1.Click

lst1.Clear()

' Para menos lío: lst1.Add(My.Resources.ListaPalabras) o un archivo alojado en otro dispositivo.
lst1.Add(My.Resources.ResourceManager.GetObject(ComboBoxResources.Text))

hset.Clear()
stbl.Clear()

' Bucle para pasar la lista de palabras donde buscar a string,
' más apto para manipular textos muy extensos.
For Each sb As String In lst1.ToArray()
stbl.Append(sb)
Next

'Variable, que uso yo, con el código de la Expresión Regular para buscar en la lista de palabras.
strg = "^[" & Palabra.Text & "]{" & CantidadMinima.Text & "," & Palabra.Lines(0).Length & "}\r$"

'Ejemplo de Expresión Regular. Opcional para comprensión más fácil.
'strg = "^([atajo]){3,5}\r$"

' Método con variable para almacenar el resultado encontrado de todas las líneas de la lista.
Dim matches2 = Regex.Matches(stbl.ToString(), strg, RegexOptions.Multiline)

' Bucle para encontrar las palabras deseadas.
' Pero con el inconveniente de que algunos caracteres se repiten
' más de lo necesario, que es el motivo de mi pregunta.
For Each mtch As Match In matches2
' Lista donde se almacenan todas las palabras encontradas sin repetirse ninguna.
hset.Add(mtch.ToString().Trim())
Next

' Para comprobar el resultado.
RichTextBoxResultados.Lines = hset.ToArray()

' Nota con la cantidad de palabras encontradas. Opcional.
LabelContarResultados.Text = FormatNumber(RichTextBoxResultados.Lines.Count, 0)

End Sub

Resultado de la búsqueda en mi lista:

ama aman amazona amo amomo ana anana anoa anon anona anza aza azo azon mam mama man mana manazo mano manzana manzano maoma maza mazana mazazo mazo moa momo mona mono monona monzon moza mozo nana nano nao noma nomo nomon non nona nono oma ona onza ozona ozono zana zaza zazo zoma zomo zona zonza zonzo zoo

Hay palabras válidas y otras que no. Además, Cada palabra es una línea.

Busco una solución a este problema, sin limitarme solo a las expresiones regulares; si conocen otros métodos que sean de utilidad para este caso, son bienvenidos y agradecidos.

Gracias de antemano.

items.title: When clicking on a plotOutput produced by grid.draw in a Shiny app, how do I map the click's returned normalized parent coordinates to the data space?
items.human_voice:
My eventual long-term goal is to create a Shiny dashboard with four separate plots arranged in a 2x2 grid. I wish for the panels of these plots to be aligned, while maintaining separate interactivity for each plot. The requirement for separate interactivity led me to use grobs to achieve the alignment, which I have done successfully.

However, I am now struggling to implement interactivity upon the grobs. My struggle is that I need to map the returned coordinates from input$plotClick back to the original coordinates of the data space so I can use them for interactive purposes, but I have been unsuccessful in my attempts to do so.

My understanding is that the units of the returned input$plotClick coordinates are normalized parent coordinates, which capture the click's width and height relative to the entire plot, not just the panel. I would understand how to map these normalized parent coordinates back to the data space if I could extract the bounds of the panel in normalized parent coordinates. However, because some elements of the plot are defined in relative units (null, grobwidth, and grobheight) the bounds of the panel in normalized parent coordinates are dependent on the dimensions of the viewing window, which can change.

A minimal example of this is shown by interacting with the shiny app below, in which two clicks to the same point on the plotting panel; e.g. (1, 3); can result in different normalized parent coordinates being returned if the size of the viewing window is changed.

library(tidyverse)
library(shiny)
library(grid)

p = ggplot(mapping = aes(x = c(1, 2, 3), y = c(4, 5, 6))) +
geom_point(size = 5) +
ylab("Really long horizontal axis title that makes the problem more noticeable") +
theme(axis.title.y = element_text(angle = 0))
g = ggplotGrob(p)

ui = fluidPage(
plotOutput("myPlot", click = "plotClick"),
verbatimTextOutput("clickInfo"),
"Clicking on the same point in the panel; for example, the bottom left point, (1,3); can map to different normalized parent coordinates if you change the size of your viewing window. The X coordinate is the only one affected in this case but the problem is more general."
)
server = function(input, output) {
output$myPlot = renderPlot({
grid.draw(g)
})
output$clickInfo = renderText({
paste0("Click x: ", input$plotClick$x, " , Click y: ", input$plotClick$y)
})
}
shinyApp(ui, server)

Is there a way to convert these normalized parent coordinates from a click upon a grob in a Shiny app back into the data space, either by extracting the normalized parent coordinates of the panel reactively, or by some other method I have not considered? (If there's a way that also restricts the click ability to just the panel, that would be an appreciated bonus!)

I have 2 time series in abundance that I'm modeling by a 2-level factor in mgcv , by "fSeason" (wet/dry), and following advice here, I should be splitting a test for auto-correlation by each factor level. DHARMa does have a test, but I was told it's only for a single time series. I don't think I can use the traditional AR(1) as the data are irregularly-spaced and I've never taken Bayesian statistics. Anyway, for now I'm just asking if the code AI generated is correctly identifying that I do have some, albeit weak, but significant temporal auto-correlation in the wet season. Any general advice is also welcome!

Data here.

library(mgcv)
library(gratia)
library(DHARMa)

system.time(
by <- gam(total_count ~

offset(log(area_sampled)) +

s(CYR, by = fSeason) +
fSeason +

s(sal, bs="ts", k=5) +
s(DO, bs="ts", k=5) +

s(ave_sav, by = fDiet_presence) +
fDiet_presence +

s(fSite, bs="re"),

data = shiny_toad,

df <- sort(diff(sort(as.Date(shiny_toad$Date))), decreasing = TRUE)

# 1. Generate the base simulated residuals once
res <- simulateResiduals(by)

# 2. Loop through each Season safely by manually subsetting the DHARMa object
for (Season in unique(shiny_toad$fSeason)) {

cat("\n--- Temporal Autocorrelation Test for Season:", Season, "---\n")

# Create a logical index for the current Season
Season_idx <- shiny_toad$fSeason == Season

# Copy the base DHARMa object structure
res_Season <- res

# Manually slice all internal arrays to match only this Season's rows

items.title: Where to place a validation rule that depends on data from another table in a DDD Spring Boot app?
items.human_voice:
I have a Spring Boot app structured with a domain layer that is kept free of persistence dependencies. I'm trying to place a validation rule and can't find a clean home for it.

Domain model

DatabaseEngine and ServerEngine are siblings extending an abstract EngineAsset extends Asset. Each overrides a checkConstraints() method that enforces its own invariants (calling super.checkConstraints() up the chain). These checks only use the object's own fields.

The problematic rule

For a DatabaseEngine, an agentServiceAccount is required only when the asset's type belongs to the "SQLServer" family. The catch: the family is not part of the domain object or the incoming DTO. It lives on a persistence entity (AssetTypeR), reachable only in the backend via a query like getQueries().toAssetTypeR(type).getEngineFamily(). The domain must not depend on AssetTypeR.

What I tried

Put the check inside DatabaseEngine.checkConstraints(). Fails: the domain object can't reach the family without depending on the persistence entity.

Resolve the family in the backend and set it on a transient field on the domain object before validating. This worked on create, but broke on update: on update I load the existing entity (old family, e.g. SQLServer), the transient field gets set from the old record, then I change the type to a non-SQLServer one — but the field still holds the stale SQLServer value, so the rule wrongly fires.

The correction (re-resolving family from the new type) happens during the domain→DB mapping, but checkConstraints() runs earlier during DTO→domain mapping and throws before execution ever reaches the correction.

The core problem

The rule needs data (family) that (a) the domain object can't access without breaking persistence-ignorance, and (b) must reflect the new/incoming type, not the persisted one. So it seems it can't be a self-invariant on the aggregate.

Question

For a validation rule that spans the aggregate plus data from another table, and that must validate against the incoming state on update:

Is the correct approach to move this out of the aggregate into a domain service that takes the aggregate and resolves the external data via a port/interface (implemented in the persistence layer)?

Or is there a cleaner, established pattern for feeding such external data into the aggregate so the rule can stay a self-invariant, without introducing a stale-state problem on update?

I want to keep the domain persistence-ignorant and avoid a field that can drift out of sync with type

items.title: Como fazer o Python tratar diacríticos como parte de um caractere?
items.human_voice:
Eu estou tentando separar a palavra "wɨoɾɨ̃mɨ" em sílabas. Ou seja, o output deve ser ["wɨ", "o", "ɾɨ̃", "mɨ"].

A função que está separando as palavras em sílabas procura uma vogal e recorta o trecho até essa vogal como uma sílaba.

def syllabification(word):
vowels = ["ɨ̃", "õ", "i", "ɨ", "ã", "ĩ", "á", "u", "í", "ó", "o", "e", "ẽ", "ú", "ũ", "é", "a"]
syllables = []
new_word = word[:]
while new_word != "":
found_vowel = False
for i, letter in enumerate(new_word):
if letter in vowels:
syllables.append(new_word[:i+1])
new_word = new_word[i+1:]
found_vowel = True
break
else:
continue
if not found_vowel:
break

return syllables

No entanto, o item "ɨ̃" não é considerado um caractere único, mas um caractere "ɨ" seguido por um diacrítico tilde. Dessa forma, o output que eu recebo é ['wɨ', 'o', 'ɾɨ', '̃mɨ'].

items.title: Observed cycle/iter greater than what's expected in simple x86 loop kernel
items.human_voice:
I am on a Skylake-X machine. Here's a very simple loop:

%include "events_asm.inc"

section .data
fmt: db "CYCLES = %lu, RETIRED = %lu", 10, 0

section .text

global main
extern perf_measure2

kernel:
mov rax, 1000000
xor rdi, rdi
xor rsi, rsi
xor rdx, rdx

align 32
.loop:
add rdi, rdi
sub rsi, rdi
and rdx, rdx
dec rax
jnz .loop
ret

main:
push rbp
mov rdi, kernel
mov rsi, fmt
mov rdx, CYCLES
mov rcx, RETIRED
call perf_measure2 wrt ..plt
pop rbp
ret

perf_measure2 is a simple helper that uses perf_event_open underneath to sample the two counters and print them. The program itself is meaningless, it only exists to probe CPU behavior. CYCLES is an alias to CPU_CLK_UNHALTED.THREAD_P and RETIRES is an alias to INST_RETIRED.ANY_P. Here are the numbers I am seeing for kernel:

CYCLES = 1448789, RETIRED = 5000650

dec and jnz macro-fuse and we're counting in unfused domain with INST_RETIRED.ANY_P, that's why we have ~5M instructions retired in the loop but rest assured we are executing no more than 4 micro-ops per iteration in the loop. With Skylake-X having 4 INT ALUs on p0156, I expected this to be no worse than 1c/iter despite the intra-iteration dependency from add to sub through rdi in the loop. Note that the other 3 ALU instructions are independent, so they can schedule together with a sub from a past iteration. I expected the dynamic scheduler to do this (X.0 here means instruction X, iteration 0):

c0: add.0 and.0 dec.0
c1: sub.0 add.1 and.1 dec.1 <--- steady state reached here
c2: sub.1 add.2 and.2 dec.2
...

As per my mental model, we are issuing 4 1c micro-op per cycle in the steady state so we should expect to retire 4 instructions every cycle too. But CYCLES = 1448789 seems to suggest we're closer to 1.5c/iteration. I never quite understood why that is. My hunch is that scheduler is failing to ideally schedule the instructions such that the add -> sub dependency does not become a bottleneck, but I cannot say with confidence that's the case. The results are very repeatable and the system is fairly idle. I didn't even bother pinning the thread because that changes nothing.

So, does anybody have a better idea of what's going on or am I right to speculate it's noise from the dynamic scheduler?

items.title: How do chores fit in with positive discipline?
items.human_voice:
My boys are still young (2.75 and 4.5), and they do a lot of natural helping, so I'm not entirely sure if they're ready for firm, consistent responsibilities yet, but I'm interested to know how best to make this work with positive discipline, and what age is appropriate to get chores started.

At the moment we don't force them to do any particular thing unless they've made a mess in an obvious, anti-social way. Occasionally they'll help us clean up, occasionally they say no and we clean up, for the most part we don't make a big deal about it unless it's a behavior that needs correcting.

So with positive discipline I'm interested in understanding what the most appropriate way is to make this non-dramatic approach work when they're older and they refuse to do some of their chores. My wife and I are both agreed that we don't want to tie their chores to an allowance, because cleaning and organizing is just a part of life that they need to learn.

But that leads to the question of: what exactly do we do in response to the situation where they aren't doing their chores or fulfilling some of their responsibilities? We don't want to punish them in a hurtful way, or force them, but we do want to teach them personal responsibility. So what would be an appropriate way to encourage fulfilling their responsibilities without negative reinforcement?

menu = {"コーヒー" => 300, "カフェラテ" => 400}から全キーを持つ配列(["コーヒー","カフェラテ"])を作ってください

menu = {"コーヒー" => 300, "カフェラテ" => 400}
keys = []

end

menu = {"コーヒー" => 300, "カフェラテ" => 400}
keys = []
menu.each do |key|
keys.push(key)
end

p keys # -> [["コーヒー",300],["カフェラテ",400]]

空の配列keysに変数menuのkey"コーヒー"と"カフェラテ"だけが格納される理由

items.title: pleiades eclipse 横に長い(一画面で収まらない)コードを書いた時のエディタのバグについて
items.human_voice:
pleiades eclipseにて

横に長い(一画面で収まらない)コードを書いた状態で、コードの最後尾あたりに文字を入力したときに、画面がコードの先頭に勝手に移動します。カーソルは移動しません。そのため、新たな文字の入力などの操作をした場合は入力している部分に画面が再度移動しますが、連続的な操作をやめると、またコードの先頭に画面が移動します。

How much should I make ADHD 8 year old work to solve puzzles before I give hints?
items.human_voice:
My 8 year old, soon to be 9, niece loves lateral thinking puzzles and has been asking me for them regularly. For context these are puzzles where you are given a strange situation and have to figure out what is happening with only yes or no questions. They usually involve at least one 'lateral leap', ie realizing something unintuitive or an intentional trick hidden within the puzzle to solve them as well.

She's liked them ever since she solved her first one years ago - she got lots of hints but considering how young she was then it was pretty impressive she solved it at all so I praised her for it. Just yesterday she was practically shouting in glee that the kid in my puzzle was blind when she finally figured out why the child 'never saw his father again'; but she only got there once I started getting pretty helpful and volunteering extra details I'm not suppose to give to her questions designed to get her to realize her presumption that something bad happened to the father couldn't be right.

She is pretty good at solving the 'lateral leap', for her age at least. Her biggest problem is that she wants to leap straight to guessing the answer. while more complicated puzzles usually require starting with more general questions designed to narrow down the situation and get more detail before one knows enough to have a realistic chance of solving the puzzle. I've been trying to tell her this and encourage her to start asking more of these generalized questions rather then trying to jump to the solution, with limited success.

Right now my biggest problem is she gets frustrated and starts asking for hints quickly. If she can't solve it all in one go she wants a hint to point her in the right direction rather then working towards methodically asking questions to expand her understanding of the situation. I like how the puzzles engage her problem solving skills, but feel she would get more out of them if I pushed her to work more to try and solve her confusion herself before she get's hints; but I don't want to make the puzzles so frustrating for her that she stops wanting to do them.

I also have the problem that I can't provide puzzles fast enough to satisfy her. I'd dare say I'm pretty decent at coming up with these sorts of puzzles, but she goes through them so quickly, thanks partially to all the hints she demands, that I just can't come up with puzzles fast enough to keep up with her demands and I'm starting to struggle with finding new puzzles she hasn't heard yet online to supplement the ones I create at this point. If we don't slow her down somehow I'm going to reach a point where I simply have no puzzles to offer her soon.

My biggest problem is that when I delay hints she starts begging for them more and more or just declare she gives up and want's the answer rather then continuing to try to solve the puzzle. I've tried to explain the steps to get better at solving the puzzles, even giving 'hints' that were basically to ask more questions about a specific subject since that would lead to more information. But my niece still tends to demand instant gratification and doesn't seem to want to try if she can't guess the answer all at once.

I should probably mention she is ADHD and by the time we get to puzzles her medication has usually worn off and she's hyperactive, which no doubt contributes to her inpatients.

So how much work should she have to put in to before she get's help, and how do I keep her engaged and interested when I delay giving her hints?

items.title: 管理者権限付きネットワークドライブの割り当てをタスクスケジューラで行う方法
items.human_voice:
管理者権限付きネットワークドライブの割り当てをタスクスケジューラで行うために方法を模索しているのですが、行き詰っています。どなたか解決方法をご存じでしたらご教示願います。

やりたいこと
PC(以下PC1とします)から自宅LAN内の別PC(以下PC2とします)上のドライブパスをネットワークドライブとして利用しようとしています。

その際、PC1で管理者権限つきで起動しているアプリケーションからもアクセスする必要があります。

毎回手動で実行するのは手間なので、タスクスケジューラにbatファイルの実行を設定して管理者権限でマウントを自動化したいと考えています。

実施したこと

下記batを作成してログオン時に実行するようタスクスケジューラに設定しました。

@echo off
if not “%~0″==”%~dp0.\%~nx0″ start /min cmd /c,”%~dp0.\%~nx0” %* & goto :eof

net use D: \\PC2\<Path_to_share>

タスクスケジューラの設定:

トリガー: ログオン時
操作: プログラムの開始: 上記batのpath
タスク実行時に使うユーザーアカウント: ログインユーザーと同じ
最上位の特権で実行するにチェック

PC1のネットワークドライブとしてD:に\\PC2\\<Path_to_share>を設定し、サインイン時に再接続するにチェックを入れました。

起きていること
D:にネットワークドライブが起動時にマウントされ、エクスプローラから参照可能な状態にはなっているのですが、管理者権限で開いたアプリケーションから当該のD:上のパスを開くとエラーとなります。

実施したことの2.に記載した設定は成功していますが、1.に記載した設定が上手く行っていないと思われます。

また、上記batを管理者権限で実行してもコマンドは正常に終了しましたと表示されるだけで問題は解決せず、管理者権限で実行したWindows Terminal上のPowerShellでnet use D: \\PC2\<Path_to_share>のコマンドを実行すると解決することを確認済みです。

class ManagerRouter:
"""

route_app_labels = {"distributor_api", "manager_api"}

echo "studyJSディレクトリを作成しました"

echo "studyJSの中に入りました"

However, she tends to skip the sessions occasionally, or she delays joining the sessions, attending very late. Over that, her parents expect me to be available any time to teach her because they reside very near to me and they expect that their daughter can come anytime to me and I will teach her, or make up for her missed sessions, etc.

After my session is skipped, her parents also expect that I make up for the session that she misses and manage to get me to agree by speaking in a way that's very clever and persuades me to allow it.

I was stunned. Being her father, doesn't he know that his daughter is not being disciplined and punctual in attending my tutoring sessions? Is it not his responsibility as her parent? In fact, he is the one who gave her the freedom and flexibility to come to my tutoring sessions at any time she wants because she resides nearby, ruining all her discipline and sense of commitment to attend the sessions sincerely and study.

I somehow think that my efforts, time and availability are taken for granted. I am thinking that her father and mother think that I will do anything that they say and adapt according to their requests. items.title: コンパイルエラーになるはずなのにeclipseでコンパイルエラーにならず、正常に結果が出力されてしまいます
Linuxのsystemdでプログラムを自動起動したい
items.human_voice:
大学でラズパイを使った研究をしている者です。タイトルの通り、作ったプログラムを、ラズパイ本体起動時に自動で実行してくれるようにしたいです。当初はcronでやろうとしてましたが、@rebootがなかったのと、定期実行だとプログラムが止まってしまうため、systemdでの自動実行を試みています。しかし、いくつかのサイトを参考に下記のように書いてみたものの、うまく動いてくれません。

[Unit]
Description = auto attendance management system

[Service]
ExecStart = /media/admin/A11E-91494/raspresarch/Gakuseisyo.py
Restart = on-failure
Type = simple

[Install]
WantedBy = multi-user.target

この状態で、enableにしても、Active:failedとなってしまいます。

statusを見てみると、

autoboot.service: Failed whit result 'exit-code'

とあったので調べてみたところ、SELinuxによる権限エラーの可能性が高いそうなので、これを無効化するコマンドやら、ファイルの書き換えやらを試しました。しかし、

SELUNUX=disabele

にしても何も変わらず、getenforceなどのコマンドは、bashされてしまいます。

初学者の私には、これ以上サイトで調べても解決できそうにありません。もしかしたら、そもそもの前提が違う可能性もありますが、ご容赦ください。最終目標は、プログラムを本体起動時に自動で実行することであるため、それがかなうならsystemdでなくても構いません。有識者の知識をお借りできますよう、お願いいたします。

items.title: Recruiter scheduled interview without confirming my availability and missed the calls – is this normal?
items.human_voice:
TL;DR: I was scheduled for a phone/Zoom interview without ever confirming my availability.

The recruiter missed the agreed‑upon times twice, never sent a Zoom link, and only responded after I followed up. I’m looking for an HR/recruiting perspective on whether this is a systemic/process issue, a one‑off human error, and what, if anything, a candidate can reasonably do—including whether contacting the recruiter’s manager is advisable.

Hi all,
I’m hoping to get a professional HR / recruiting perspective on a situation I experienced, to understand whether there may be a reasonable explanation I’m missing.

What happened

No invitation to pick a time. I never received an email asking me to select interview availability.

First scheduling email: I got a confirmation that the recruiter would call my phone at a specific time. No Zoom/Teams link was included.

First interview: No call came through at the scheduled time. I emailed to check in. The recruiter replied that they were “waiting for me on Zoom,” even though no Zoom link had been provided.

First reschedule: We agreed on a new date and time. The follow‑up email again did not state whether the interview would be a phone call or a video call, nor did it contain a link.

Second follow‑up: I asked explicitly, “Will this be a phone call or a Zoom call?” and received no response.

Second interview: Again, no call came through at the agreed time.

After I followed up a second time, the recruiter finally said the interview had to be on Zoom but that they could not join because of laptop issues, and asked to reschedule once more.

Third scheduling email: This time a Zoom link was finally included and the interview is scheduled for next week.

What I’m trying to understand

It's possible that a lapse in professionalism could explain the first scheduling email, but that alone doesn't seem to account for the later missed calls and the presistent lack of clarification. While I suspect there may be factors beyond simple sloppiness, I'm open to hearing other explanations.

I'm planning to cancel the interview but wondering if it's appropriate for a candidate to email the recruiter’s manager (or the talent‑acquisition lead) after repeated missed interviews? If so, what is the best way to phrase such a message while staying professional?

items.title: clangでADLを使おうとすると警告されるのはなぜ？
Concerns regarding team escalation practices and collaboration challenges
items.human_voice:
I am the most senior engineer in the team

Recently, a junior team member asked me to add them to the admin group for a credential store that I had created last year. I explained that project-specific credential stores cannot be accessed by other projects and suggested that if the team plans to use a global store, it would allow cross-project access. I also requested confirmation on their approach. (In my opinion, if they create a global store, I wouldn’t need to take any action, which would save time.)

Instead of confirming their plans, the junior escalated the request privately to the manager. In a team meeting, the manager framed it as if I were blocking the task. The technical concerns I raised about potential errors were not evaluated, and no clarification was sought from the junior. Despite this, I was directed to add them to the admin group, while the responsibility for addressing potential errors was left with the junior.

Later, I clarified that project-specific admin access can only be granted by the business owner, not by me. Despite this clarification, my manager seems to perceive my intentions as being driven by reluctance or ego.

If I express that performing an action that I know will cause errors is a waste of time, the manager becomes irritated; for example, once she remarked, “Do you think you are the President of (country-name)?”

I’ve noticed a pattern where escalations bypass discussion and create misunderstandings about intent. Any escalation by a junior's is not evaluated by the manager to determine whether it is genuine or a result of bypassing their own work. This has affected team culture, as new members now communicate more through directives than collaborative discussions. I am concerned that repeated public escalations and criticism may undermine respect and effective collaboration in the team. If the manager insults me in front of everyone, it becomes difficult for the team to respect me.

items.title: Acting in the face of unrealistic expectations
items.human_voice:
Related: How to handle unrealistic expectations from management

Here's how it should be:

You collect your customers' needs.
You analyze those needs and convert them to epics, user stories, tasks.
You complete those.
You test.
You deploy.

Here's how it (often) happens in our company.

We deploy.
Then customers announce some additional requirements.
Then we're hustling to meet those requirements. Devs, like myself, get urgent requests: "Quick! Develop this feature ASAP! We need to close the contract!"
There's no time to develop it properly, let alone test it. Our QA is understaffed (basically, one person and a lead), so you either skip QA altogether (it's not required, you as a developer decide whether to involve the QA or deploy it right away yourself) or take more time than they are happy to allocate. In other words, there's a slower, safer approach and a faster, riskier approach. They want it good and fast. Either way, you're under a lot of pressure and likely to draw criticism, for either being too slow or creating buggy software. There is no guaranteed extra compensation for that.

Note tasks do not necessarily have a fixed scope, so providing an estimate is not really possible. Also, giving a realistic estimate is perceived as a rejection to do the job (which is to do it quick) and is not met nicely by our lead. I wish he stood up for us and our professional standards, but he just channels the pressure the management puts on him onto us.

How do you act professionally in situations like this as a developer?

items.title: Four Year Old Pushing and Positive Discipline Techniques
items.human_voice:
This isn't a major problem for us, but I'm curious to get a few perspectives on this issue. My wife and I have two boys, two and four, both close to two and four, and for the most part we try to use positive discipline techniques to correct their behavior. So far we don't really punish them, although we'll very occasionally raise our voice in a targeted way (usually only for the four year old at this point). We try to teach and mentor them into better behavior, rather than making them feel bad about things they've done.

I think, for the most part, this has been successful and we've seen real improvements in self regulation in the four year old. He's very independent, and I would call him mature for his age. The two year old is too young to see much difference.

However, occasionally the four year old will do something a little over the line like push younger brother completely unprompted, and in his last months at daycare he's really starting to test the educators. This is where the question comes in. A part of me thinks: this is all age appropriate for the most part, and he'll gradually grow out of it in the next few years. But he is becoming a little more brazen, and you can tell that he's becoming comfortable testing boundaries because there are no real repercussions to his behavior. For the most part he's well behaved, but when he wants to break a rule he'll break a rule.

So then that leads to the question: do we introduce some kind of mild deterrent to encourage him to stop doing things like pushing his brother, or other ridiculous / dangerous stuff. Something like no TV for the night. Would that kind of thing be age appropriate, or does his behavior come down to not having the ability to fully self regulate?

She was relaxing and didn't want to be bothered, so as frequently happens, she started saying no and trying to push him away from her. I didn't say anything immediately, because as mentioned, it is a frequent source of family discord, so I try to choose my battles. Shortly after, when mother was back in the room, I brought it up with her and asked her to have a conversation with him, because I considered it inappropriate. She got angry at me and told me I only thought it was inappropriate because he was not my son, that if he was my son I would not have a problem with it; and because I was raised by strict, religious, prudish parents (which is true, although I have not been religious myself for decades now, and don't feel that I am prudish).

My question is basically, is it normal or okay for a boy of that age to be licking his younger sister like that? items.title: Linuxのポートフォワードで外部からのアクセスを許可したい
items.human_voice:
あるアプリケーションがあり、それはローカルサーバーを起動します。

その際、リッスンするのは localhost で、ポートは 3000 番で固定です。

これはオプションにより変更はできません。

このサーバーに 80 番ポートで、同じネットワークの別の端末からのアクセスをできるようしたいです。

現在一応動く形にはできたもののあまり良い方法と思えないのでより良い手段があれば教えていただきたいです。

現在の方法は、 ssh のポートフォワード機能を使っています。

自分自身に ssh で接続し、ローカルフォワードと -g オプションを使い、 80 番ポートのアクセスを 3000 番ポートにフォワードしています。

別の試した方法ですが、 iptables や firewalld でもポートフォワードはできるようで、その環境では firewalld が有効になっていたので、 firewalld を使う方法を試してみたのですが、 firewalld を使う場合は 0.0.0.0 のリッスンとはならないようで、同端末から localhost ではアクセスできるものの外部からはアクセスできません。

なにかいい方法があれば教えていただけると幸いです。

追記）

使用するツールは、できれば RHEL 系で初期から入ってるもの、難しければ dnf にてインストール可なものとしたいです。

dnf では RHEL のパッケージと EPEL が使えます。

items.title: Referee says she'll try to support me "this one time"

it’s me again, [name]. I’m in [western european country], and things aren’t 100% settled yet, but it looks like I’ll most likely be staying here.

Warm regards and all the best for the future

June and August: one or two employers contacted the catholic community service centre for employment references in relation to roles in domestic work where I was too slow with the onboarding process to be taken on, unfortunately.

Beginning of December: reference request from receptionist of employer in a sector I'm much more enthusiastic about, in parallel with an automatic reference request from employer HR, probably sent to the catholic community service centre email and intended for Supervisor.

15 December, 08:00, to Supervisor

Hi [Supervisor],

I hope you, [name], [name], [name], and everyone else are doing well. items.title: Adressing/introducing Autism
items.human_voice:
So my 10yo son has recently been diagnosed with functioning autism. It has been a big relief for us to actually understand what he is experiencing - he would pace a lot, very fixated on destructive thoughts as entertaining, ("and then imagine if it just blew up!"), would get agitated seemingly out of nowhere, etc. It was frustrating for everyone because no one knew what the issues were, and he would be unable to explain. Now that we understand, we can then solve the issues.

However what I am struggling with is telling him that he has autism. One of his biggest habits is latching on to labels. He would use them as excuses for behaviours. For example dealing with self control, he would not fix the self control, regardless of the direction, and motivation we might give him, address and readdress, he would simply blame the "lack of self control".

In the same way I don't want him to identify himself as autistic, and use that as a label by which to limit himself.

For example, I myself have epilepsy. However it is not something I use to identify myself, it's just a part of my life. I take medication, I avoid triggers and I keep aware of any potential syndromes, but otherwise I live my life as per normal. I do not limit myself by my epilepsy.

How can I address this with my son, in a way that he understands that he is not an autistic person, but a person that has autism?

items.title: potty training sibling of an autistic child
items.human_voice:
We have two kids (in 8 mos, we will have three). Our daughter is 4, diagnosed autistic. Our son is 2.5--never assessed, but does not appear to be autistic (displays no visible to us symptoms).

While we lived in NY, due to state budget issues, she had no access to services until this past Jan (and it wasn't even full services that she was supposed to receive), so we had no prof assistance with her and her behavior was very difficult (she was unresponsive to most direction and would routinely lash out, especially at her brother).

Despite this, over the course of about a year, we got her to pee in her potty. Her brother, whom we began training around same time, achieved same degree of success of peeing in potty. A month ago, we moved from NY to Illinois. The move severely shocked our daughter, and the first two weeks, she was tremendously combative and physically aggressive, especially with her brother. She hardcore refused to use the potty and we decided not to wage that battle. Two weeks ago, she was admitted into the school system and at last, began to receive full services. Her behavior improved and we are resuming potty training. Unfortunately, not only are we at ground zero with her on potty training, but also with him, as during our first two weeks here, while she was aggressive, he too began to refuse using the potty. So we are starting from scratch with him as well.

My question is this: should we attempt to,
either on our own or with professional assistance, speed track the potty training process with him (regardless of her rate of progress)
or
is it better to go back to the beginning and let it take how long it takes?

Any additional thoughts appreciated.

items.title: Collaborating with management when the company's undetailed directives seem irrational?
items.human_voice:
Background
I'm an I.T. guy (software architect and technical expert, "firefighter of incidents") who works best with:

explanations and big picture

When having an incident to handle, rather than (outdated) specifications I prefer relying on end users and technical operators explaining me their actual problem and constraints
consistency

I'm not looking to solve individual problems, I'm making sure every addition / solution works well with, and benefits to, existing parts of software (e.g. expanding existing workflows to handle new subcases, rather than adding a whole new workflow)
continuity

Proudly enriching software (and relations) I built 5 years ago, rather than scraping everything every 2 years

Not only do I need to exert those 3 points, but lack of them becomes harmful (I waste lots of energy on unlogical, segmented, weather vane directives, trying to find back an underlying logic and ending up squaring the circle).

The hickup
However, what has worked well in my daily job reaches its limits when confronted to top-down company policies.
I never managed to integrate seemingly ever-changing guidelines in my way of thinking (while I consider myself usually adaptable).

How can I enter the company's logic when I feel it wreaks havoc regarding my 3 requirements?

I'm looking for tips / strategies to enter a collaborative mode, transforming the glass ceiling into a plasma membrane, so that:

management can simply explain me the company's strategy
I can adopt those new constraints in my cartesian "big picture" (of everything that needs to be taken into account, to stay competitive and thus continue satisfying customers and employees for years, which is my personal end goal)
(but be heard too in that this has a cost on the morale of people like me, who may see it as steps backwards against their past efforts to fulfill the previous, now contradictory, rules)
everybody can then work optimally (according to their talents: management on strategy, operationals within their area of expertise) contributing to shared goals

What I've tried

mocking those programs

doesn't solve the problem, but helps decompressing with similarly thinking colleagues
passive resistance

waiting (with aforementioned colleagues) for the policy to revert next year, continuing to work with what seems to us common sense inbetween
naively asking the management to explain me the strategy and how it could articulate with daily tasks and individual objectives

So far this (honesty) seems to me the right way, however it didn't pay off (see "glass ceiling" in the hickup §, and "architects" in the examples §).

… OK, maybe I tried after 1. and 2., with management not eager to listen to me anymore

Examples
Past real examples at my company:

Architects: generalists or specialists?
While in the midst of a reorganization that I deplored (all cross-system architects being grouped in one entity, while previously we had one department of architects dedicated to B2B systems, one dedicated to B2C, and one dedicated to interconnection with partners and competing companies),

an auditing firm presented the results of a year-long study saying in essence "now instead of teams grouped by technical skills, the IT Department will dedicate small, versatile teams to each functional business unit".

Talking to my manager "Well, it seems this goes against the reorganization, and in line with my thoughts, doesn't it? — In theory yes", she replied, embarassed, "but… well that's the way it is, the IT Dept won't go back, stick with it.". End of conversation.

Diversity
Team-building exercise: "This year's objective is Diversity, so to understand how rich our team is from its diversity, and also how many we can hurt by seemingly harmless remarks, we'll silently raise hands each time we feel concerned by one of the following sentences: 1. I cannot eat everything (vegan, gluten, …). 2. At school I felt rejected for my physical appearance. 3. I feel religious. 4. I have an invisible disability." And so on.

This was an enlightening exercise… but it came right while in the process of trying to find me a new position with my HR, after having agreed that my profile (meeting people in small task forces, sometimes directly contacting customers, to solve problems, instead of relying on specifications and big room meetings with only IT people) hardly fit anymore with the company's rationalization effort ("either be a technical expert, an architect, or a support guy").

Too different to fit, but not enough to be seen as a complementary richness for the team?

Programs
Year 2020's program was "Go to Cloud":

go ahead, ask for a lot of virtual machines, start them even if they're used 10 mn in a day;

when I asked about their cost compared to on-premise machines, one of the FinOps guy told me that "it's too complex to tell, so to simplify projects managers are told it costs 0".

Year 2022 was "Green IT":

where can we improve our carbon footprint?

(I arrived too late to participate the brainstorming team, but I could submit that perhaps simply looking at 2020's open bar excesses would be a good starting point)

Year 2024 was "AI everywhere":

At the time I didn't know how energy-hungry AI was, but it seems neither did the decision makers who probably were the same people as for "Green IT"…

Why my question still matters
N.B.: I'm no longer employed, as the HR and I agreed I would fit no other position in the company (whose "rationalization reorganization" was global). So I have the opportunity to start from scratch, and "find a company with less levels of management" would be a perfectly valid answer.

However I feel that:

not everyone can afford changing job, so advice on how to transform ourselves, and the mentalities, in an existing structure, would be of interest to many
on a personal point of view, I retrospectively would like to understand what I could have done better; and anyhow, I'll probably look for a big company (with plenty of customers to unlock, and lots of diversity in the problems!), so I'll make good use of advice on how to act in a big structure with high inertia.

items.title: What to do in the moment when a toddler falls asleep so late for his nap that it folds into his bedtime?
items.human_voice:

I've seen plenty of advice for how to fix a sleep schedule after such an event occurs - which is well and fine, but what I need more than anything in a situation like that is to know what to do in the moment when he's overslept his nap.

items.title: 6 year old aggressive and impulsive behavior
items.human_voice:
My 6 year old stepson has shown signs of ADHD for many years. The worst of it is shown in school, where the behaviors are out of control. He has extra help and support from staff and teachers who give him breaks throughout the day. However nothing works. He has gotten suspended from school over 15 times, they have gotten to the point of possibly kicking him out. The suspensions are due to him biting, pushing, hitting and choking other children.

We have tried behavior charts, reward system, time outs, extra breaks out of structured time. We limit the stuff he watches and plays with and he's never been around or seen any violent things to where he would pick up this behavior. This behavior of aggressiveness only seems to be a problem around his classmates because he does not show aggression to us or older adults. We understand he struggled with impulsive control and ADHD so we try to give him extra support and understanding.

I’m not sure what to do anymore. We have tried getting him into a program for children who struggle with ADHD, but they say he’s too young. We are on the waitlist for a therapist and many other programs when a spot opens up. We do discipline him such as taking away toys and not doing fun things and not allowing screen time, but I’m not sure how much this works because I don’t think his mother follows through with the same routine we do. items.title: Force 9-year old to finish what he started?
items.human_voice:
A few months ago, I subscribed my 9 year old son to a code learning platform for kids, to try to give him a taste for logic and technology.
During that same period, he asked me for a game console.
I took the opportunity and told him if he finished the entire coding course, he’d get a console.
At first, he was excited and kept asking for more. Little by little the tasks became more difficult and he played less and less. And the less he practiced, the more difficult it became. Now he’s really not enjoying it and gets frustrated a lot.

Now, he asked me if I could give him a different challenge to get his game console.
I’m hesitant:
On one hand I want to respect that he’s not obligated to like the things I like, and don’t want to force him.
On the other hand, I don’t want him to quit things in life just when they get a little difficult.

items.title: Advanced Placement and Honors classes
items.human_voice:

My daughter is an advanced learner. Her freshman year of high school, her lowest grade is 97%. She can start taking Honors classes next year and AP classes as a junior. Although I think AP classes are great for college credit, I have hesitation about Honors.

Her HS does not weight the courses, so it’s the same 4.0 for an A in an Honors course compared to a non-Honors course also receiving a 4.0. Her likelihood of straight As in Honors (or more than two APs) is greatly diminished.

items.title: Manager emails a list of employees who have not yet completed a training module. Is this a labor violation of any kind?
items.human_voice:
A manager at my workplace has grown understandably frustrated over time due to frequent non-compliance with periodic mandatory training modules. The trainings are typical things you'd see in any work place: sexual harrassment prevention, data security, avoiding scams, etc. This manager's new tactic is to publicly publish, via a daily email, a list of all who have not yet completed an item, beginning one week prior to the deadline. The email distribution is not the entire company, but the subset that works at our given location.

I know that this tactic is immoral and represents weak leadership. The use of shame and humiliation is never the right answer to any problem. But does it actually violate any labor or privacy policies or laws? I plan to take my concerns to HR, but want to be prepared with any information that can bolster my objections.

For additional context, I am at one of several US location of a US, Canada, and India company. If this question would be a better fit at Law SE, let me know I will self-close and re-ask there.

Edits to answer some comments:

Specific state is Michigan
I have completed all training. I am receiving the emails which list others who have not. I will not be reading these emails. My concerns are on behalf of those listed.
Of course all of us have access to each others' names, email addresses, team assignments, title, and more. We do not normally have access to each others' training records, however, nor whether taken on time versus late.
The immediate consequence of failure to complete includes being locked out from certain systems until completed. Termination would not occur until much later.
The manager in question is upper-level. In the past, this person has handled things by reaching out to each individual's direct manager to deal with. This tactic of a wide spread and public list is new. The change from handling mostly privately to handling entirely publicly is what I object to.

items.title: Rough and tumble play with 1.5 yo son turns to actual voilent behavior
items.human_voice:
I have the feeling that my one-and-a-half-year-old son often wants to play wildly in the evenings or even have a kind of tussle. However, this almost exclusively follows the pattern that it is initially a kind of tickling and light tossing around, but after a few minutes it turns into violent scratching, nipping and biting on his part. He laughs at first, but the mood quickly changes when I make it clear that it hurts me and that I won't continue playing like this.

My son is very cuddly and very focussed on my wife. She has a much calmer way of playing with him. In addition to roughhousing, he also occasionally demands affectionate closeness, although he mainly seeks this from my wife, as he is also breastfed in the evening. I don't see this problem with my two years older daughter, who also seems more calm and prefers things to be less wild.

I realise that children of this age like to test boundaries and are not yet capable of much empathy, but I still wonder whether it is possible to teach the boundaries between friendly roughhousing and actually hurting without overtaxing the child. Or would it be better to avoid playing too rough altogether?

items.title: Informally suggesting leadership change to management
items.human_voice:
A very experienced AQA (Automated Quality Assurance) has recently left our company (7 years in the company, 5 of which in the QA (Quality Assurance)); the context here is in software testing. Let's call her Helen. She's not been treated very fairly lately and was underpaid hugely.

She found a slightly higher-paying but less satisfactory job. It's not QA or development at all and doesn't employ any of her skills. A few months in, Helen's now considering looking for a new job again. If she decided to stay in the AQA, I'm sure she could get even more.

Unfortunately, while being a great professional and a great person, she sucks at job search. First, she applies way less than she should (I think she did like a couple of applications or so before finding her current job, she deliberates over each job posting, and not in a good way). Second, she doesn't want to use her great experience and seek an AQA position. In fact, she's not very consistent at what she wants at all. One time, she says she wants to be an SQL developer; another time, she says she wants to be NodeJS developer. She has little experience with the former and no experience with the latter. Switching careers is great, but, I believe, not in the current job market.

While not being thrilled about seeking a new AQA position, Helen would be happy to rejoin the company in the same role if it offered her at least as much compensation. She misses the company (I think she shouldn't and she should move on, but here we are).

Our QA department is not doing very well, especially since Helen's departure. Helen's less experienced successor has now left too, partly due to too much pressure. The remaining QA has almost left too (she had a pretty good offer on hand). One of the factors is the subpar leadership ability of the department's current lead. Let's call him Bill. He's put way too much pressure on the girls and at times been disrespectful to them. I know it for a fact since I communicated with all of them.

I'm a rank-and-file developer in that company, in a different department. I'm considering texting to a person in charge of things and suggesting offering Bill's position to Helen. Bill could perform some managerial role instead (I don't have anything specific in mind). I want it to proceed only if both of them agree. Helen is almost certainly going to accept it. I'm not sure about Bill.

Here's why it may be a good idea.

Helen would almost certainly be a better QA lead.

She got technical skills – something Bill doesn't have.
She's not toxic and treats people with more respect.

The company is stingy – and yet it may be more willing to offer Helen more money if she takes a more senior position (at least I hope so).
While I believe Helen deserves a lot more than what the company can offer her, with her method of looking for job, her chances of getting a good offer are next to zero (I tried to persuade her to change her approach, but she's somewhat stubborn). With that in mind, she may indeed be better off returning to our company on better terms.

Here's why it may be a bad idea.

It may be bad for Bill. While I believe he's made mistakes, I don't think he's an evil man, and I wish him no harm. I'm concerned my plan may get of hand, "Wait, I didn't mean him to get fired!" Like Helen whom I'm worried about, Bill got kids to feed, and it may not be very easy to find a new job now. It may be the straw that breaks the camel's back if they are already concerned about his leadership skills due to recent departures (I don't know if that's the case, but it may very well be).
Some may argue I would be stepping out of line. I'm not a big worshipper of "lines", but I'm throwing this item on the list nonetheless. After all, it's just a suggestion. I'm not the one who's calling the shots in the end.

I wouldn't be asking this if I didn't believe my plan could work (for better or worse).

I declare no conflict of interest, though I did have a small argument with Bill a few weeks ago, when he decided he could tell me what I "must" do or not do in our code. Actually, he had zero authority over it, and their flaky tests were to blame – but it's a different story.

What do you think I should do?

items.title: Can I Say No to Overtime During My Notice Period? And shift the responsibility on Manager?
items.human_voice:
I'm currently in my notice period, working in an offshore delivery role from India. I’m part of an ongoing project where the workload has recently spiked beyond initial estimates.

Early on, I raised this concern with my manager. Unfortunately, instead of addressing the issue, he reassigned one of our key contributors to another initiative — ironically, one that I also lead but has no urgent deadlines. In return, I was given a new team member. While I was skeptical at first, he’s performed well and adapted quickly. As it stands, we are a team of three and making reasonable progress.

To ensure clarity, I sent an email outlining realistic delivery timelines based strictly on regular working hours. This email was shared with my manager, the offshore manager, and the broader team. I also made it clear that, during my notice period, I’m not available for overtime. No one raised any concerns at the time.

Now, a week later, the workload has gone up again. I flagged this to my manager, but there has been no meaningful acknowledgment of the fact that I’m not working beyond normal hours — even though the tasks are now being labeled as “urgent.”

Here’s where I’m conflicted:

Since I’ve already made my stance clear about working hours, do I need to restate it more firmly?

Given that I only have 6 weeks left and this increased workload is likely to last just 2 more weeks, is the team simply choosing to ignore the issue in the hope things will get done regardless?

At this stage, is it still my responsibility to worry about delivery timelines or resource planning, especially when no one seems to be taking ownership?

I’m also concerned that the manager may assign a fresher to the project to "help," but in reality, that could slow things down due to onboarding and lack of relevant experience.

I’ve done my part to highlight risks, proposed timelines, and flagged concerns early. But if no action is taken by the relevant stakeholders, should I just stop worrying about it and focus solely on my assigned work within regular hours?

I’m keen on ensuring a smooth and professional exit, but not at the cost of burnout or personal commitments.

Has anyone else faced this situation during their notice period? How did you handle it?

This is an edited post and not similar to another post which was flagged earlier. The core issue is completely different.

items.title: Co-Lead Role Undermined, Manager Dismissive
items.human_voice:
I’m hoping to get some perspective or advice from others who’ve navigated similar challenges. I’ve been a customer experience designer for over 15 years, and I’ve spent the last six years with my current employer—three of those on a small but high-impact team that serves thousands of customers across the enterprise.

About 18 months ago, I was assigned as a co-lead on a new software project alongside a colleague with similar experience. We split responsibilities: she focused on visual design, while I handled project management and operations. At first, things were fine. But soon, she began taking on tasks assigned to me—without informing me. I wasn’t out of office or behind schedule. This led to me giving inaccurate updates to stakeholders, only to be contradicted in meetings or told by clients that decisions had already been made with her.

When I raised concerns, she said she “thought she told me” and was “sorry I felt left out.” I tried to be collaborative: I asked to be looped into relevant meetings, worked with her and our program manager to define clearer workflows, and even offered to redistribute responsibilities. She declined, saying she was overwhelmed.

Despite these efforts, the behavior continued. I documented each incident and eventually brought it to my manager—someone I had always considered fair. Unfortunately, she sided with my coworker, calling her a “team player” and labeling me “unprofessional.” When I pointed out that my coworker had been upset when I covered her tasks during her PTO, the inconsistency was ignored. I asked for a formal outline of our roles, which my manager provided—but only for me, and with language that felt dismissive and demeaning.

I’ve been job hunting for over three years, ever since our company was acquired. But I can’t afford a pay cut. I live paycheck-to-paycheck, carry decades-old student loan debt, and support my mother’s memory care. I have no savings or emergency fund. Quitting isn’t an option.

Now, I have a meeting scheduled Tuesday morning to review the responsibilities document. I’ve always gone above and beyond, invested in my own development, and genuinely loved my work. But lately, I feel physically ill just thinking about going in.

Has anyone else been in a situation like this—where your role is undermined, leadership is dismissive, and you feel trapped financially and professionally? What helped you move forward?

items.title: My superiors want me to pretend in front of my subordinates that I support a company policy I disagree with. How do I handle this instruction?
items.human_voice:
I am the leader (say, level 3) of a small team of engineers (level 4), one of many in our project.

A couple of months ago, our management (level 1), together with HR, has announced plans for a new organisational policy that has been met with a high degree of criticism from levels 3 and 4 (and so far, at least one senior employee of two decades quitting in response).

Many people in levels 3 and 4 in my circle of contacts - including myself - strongly oppose the policy and do not consider the reasoning put forth by level 1 to be sensible.

Our level 2 managers have explicitly confirmed level 1 management see no problem with our current work output and the change in policy has nothing to do with any issues on that end. Further, these level 2 managers have assured us their support in helping us bring forth some alternative solutions for fulfilling level 1 management's underlying wishes (if only we can figure out what these are).

Now, several months of discussion between level 1 management and various internal parties have passed. Level 1 management and HR have finally announced they are going to impose the policy regardless, all the arguments against are considered irrelevant. Fair enough, their prerogative.

Here's the problem: Level 1 management and HR have now informed levels 2 and 3 that we are now supposed to enforce the policy toward our reports. In particular, our instructions are (paraphrased):

Do not shift responsibility to someone else by pointing e.g. to management or HR. Tell your direct reports that you want them to adhere to the policy and justify to them, why this makes sense.

EDIT: To clarify: I understand the above in such a way that I have to convey the new rules and the reasoning behind them as provided by management, but without saying these rules and the reasoning come from management. In my opinion, if I cannot say "rule X is necessary because of Y, according to management", but only "rule X is necessary because of Y", that leaves no other interpretation than that I personally believe in that justification.

How do I handle this without blatantly lying to my team members' faces? As mentioned, my reports are very much aware I oppose this policy and see the reasons listed by level 1 as baseless.
