items.title: Toddler (2 1/2 year old boy) won’t sleep without mum or dad in his bedroom
items.human_voice:
Wondering if anyone has a solution for a phase we are going through with our 2 1/2 year old son. Since before he was 2, our son has had some real issues with sleeping alone in his room.

He has a pretty typical routine where:

Dinner around 6-6.30pm
Playtime 7.30-7pm
Bath time 7-7.30pm
7.30-8pm PJs on and read a book.
8-8.30pm Milk in cot to fall asleep.

The problem we are facing is that as soon we finish the book, he immediately asks for one of us to sit next to his bed or on the double bed we have in his room as he knows we are about to put him into his cot for bed time. You can actively see the anxiety on his face and hear it in his voice as soon as he knows he has to sleep and that we might leave.

The only way we can get him to sleep now is by lying in the bed in his room till he falls asleep, we then leave to go into our bedroom.

He’ll then wake up at midnight crying out and we’ll have to go in and stroke his head (we normally wait in case he falls back to sleep but he never does) until he falls asleep and then leave to go back to our bedroom.

The next wake up will be 3am and he then cries out even louder and this wake up he needs us to stay in the room with him otherwise he won’t go back to sleep. Both these wake ups are like clockwork and require the same method to get him back to sleep.

We’ve tried all the methods:

I’ll be right back - extending the returns more and more. This resulted in him becoming more worked up each time it got longer and longer.

Cry it out - walk out after saying good night and cuddles etc. we left him for over an hour crying and calling out, jumping in his cot, till we finally went in to comfort him. This was an awful experience for all of us and I don’t know if we could stomach that again.

Edging closer to the door each night. Similar to the "I’ll be right back" approach, he just got more anxious each time we got closer to the door.

Sleeping on the floor/bed and moving that closer to door. Same result as when we sat on the floor moving closer to the door, he would just get more anxious the closer we got.

If anyone has gone through this before, it would be great to hear how you dealt with this. Even to hear that you ended up just staying in their room and the phase passed, I think hearing how long it took would give us some peace knowing there is light at the end of the tunnel and knowing how long that realistically could be.

Thank you community!

Dad

items.title: Walk or Drive to school?
items.human_voice:
In Greece I see many (not as many as I see in Japanese movies) elementary school kids (6-12) walking on their own to their school. I myself almost always got drived to school (my parents never walked me to school). I only regularly walked myself to school in highschool (I was 14 because I was born in December). I am interested and curious about parental choices (maybe my parents could have done better, I am close to parenting age, seeing young children on the road leaves me wondering).

What should you do with your kids when the distance to school is less than a mile or two? Assume a relatively safe area when it comes to crimes, a slight uphill slope ~100 metres, and some navigation problems and risks of traffic accidents. How does this choice change as they grow older (probably they gain navigation skills, independence, can better manage their wake-sleep cycles)?

The options I see are three:

Walk them there
Send them off on their own
Drive them to school

Walking has the benefit of freedom of motion. (Driving a mile or two with heavy traffic is not the best thing and is unpredictable; half an hour on foot is usually half an hour while a 5-minute drive can become 15-20.) If they walk on their own they gain independence and might socialize on their way there. (It also saves you time to leave for work in the morning but the main focus is parenting.) If their parents walk them there that is safer (especially at younger ages with traffic accidents) and that is some quality time spent with the kids.

Driving can save some minutes of (their) sleep especially in the morning (unless there is a lot of traffic or you can't find a place to park).

items.title: How to prepare children for evil
items.human_voice:
I want to prepare my children for life in the best possible way (as most parents do), and an important aspect of this is, in my opinion, teaching them about the evil things humans are capable of, so that they can look for signs and try to avoid or fight it. Maybe the classic teaching in this regard is "don't take anything from strangers, don't go with them, no matter how nice they seem". But this does not tell the child what the problem really is. I believe the child is better prepared if they know what could happen if they followed the stranger. So the child should know about for example: rape, torture, drug addiction, violence because of differing sexual orientation or religion... to name a few. But they shouldn't be so terrified that they cannot function properly (like feeling the need to run away whenever a stranger talks to them).

I do think they should confront all those horrors (by reading, watching films, talking about it) in order to be prepared, but I don't know when and in what dosage. I don't want to turn them into psychic wrecks that are too afraid to leave the house, after all.

I am looking for guidelines on how to determine which kind of atrocities my child can mentally handle, and in what way (at their age or current developmental stage). Are there any parenting books on this? Or any other resources?

For movies, there are age recommendations. And the people who give out these recommendations must have some basis for their decisions. What is that basis?

To give a concrete example where I want to teach but don't know how: I have a 5 year old son. We recently listened to a happy-go-lucky children's podcast episode that was about love and affection and that two people of the same sex being affectionate towards each other is as OK as the standard male-female affection. And in the podcast it was said that "some people do not know this yet, they think only male-female is OK, so we should tell them: love is for everyone!". As if homophobia was just missing knowledge like illiteracy... My take on this is: Sure, there are people - mainly kids - who think it is not OK because they have been told so, but not reflected it in any way. But there are also many people who have CHOSEN to find it not OK, and among them still enough to readily use violence against not only those who are homosexual but also against those who promote accepting homosexuality as OK. And I want my son to know this, so that he does not run around happily-go-luckily, being blind to the evil in humans, telling men who are busy throwing gay couples from roofs that they just haven't heard the news yet. Because he will be next.
(Some might argue that the topic of homosexuality is not appropriate for a 5 year old and I tend to agree, but it is impossible - at least for me - to check every bit of media before I expose him to it (especially when I found a series to be suitable, I do not pre-watch/listen every episode), just like I cannot plan every step of his life. So at some point he will be confronted with something new, challenging, disturbing. That's why I am asking this question.)

items.title: What role does the impact of inflation have on retirement planning?
items.human_voice:
I frequently hear it said that the percentage we make on our investments slated for retirement is directly undercut by inflation numbers, and that we should outpace inflation by a reasonable margin. That is reasonable enough.

But thinking about our actual retirement expenses it doesn't look like the calculation is so clear cut. If we've already paid off our house, for example, inflation has no impact on about 20-25% of our typical expenses, reducing the impact. If we're driving less, using less hydro, buying fewer goods, buying fewer groceries, then inflations impact ends up being fairly minimal.

To me it looks like the biggest impact of inflation would be on food costs, which at worst is going to be about 20% of our total costs. Maybe insurance and energy as well.

All that said, I'd like to get a sanity check on how I should be thinking about inflation and what to consider in how it will impact retirement planning.

items.title: How to exclude a file or a folder in a robocopy two-ways backup .bat
items.human_voice:
I'm not a native English speaker. I tried to update my HDD multi-computer sync .bat to include (or in this case exclude) some files I want to remove from the backup.

For the moment the core of the .bat are 4 simple robocopy statements.

I found this solution on Stackoverflow and adapted it to my use.

The HDD is hard mapped to the P: disk on all my computers for a more practical use, and the %dest% is usually the desktop (boooh).

for %%I in (.) do set CurrDirName=%%~nxI
echo %CurrDirName%

robocopy /s /xo /dst "%CD%" "%dest%\%CurrDirName%"
robocopy /s /xo /dst "%CD%" "P:\%CurrDirName%"
robocopy /s /xo /dst "%dest%\%CurrDirName%" "%CD%"
robocopy /s /xo /dst "P:\%CurrDirName%" "%CD%"

The problem with this setup is that I can't remove any file or directory that has already been backed up, since it will be robocopied back again at each exec of the .bat.

I want to exclude any file or folder with the name ending with (r).

Here is the test setup:

\test
|...yes.txt
|...no (r).txt
|...perhaps.txt
|...\yes
|...|...yes.txt
|...|...no (r).txt
|...\no (r)
|...|...yes.txt
|...|...no (r).txt
|...\perhaps
|...|...yes.txt
|...|...no (r).txt

The "perhaps" files and folders will be manually renamed "perhaps (r)" after the first backup.

So let's work: it's easy to exclude the "no" from the robocopy command:

robocopy /s /xo /dst "%CD%" "%dest%\%CurrDirName%" /XF "* (r).*" /XD "* (r)*"
robocopy /s /xo /dst "%CD%" "P:\%CurrDirName%" /XF "* (r).*" /XD "* (r)*"
robocopy /s /xo /dst "%dest%\%CurrDirName%" "%CD%" /XF "* (r).*" /XD "* (r)*"
robocopy /s /xo /dst "P:\%CurrDirName%" "%CD%" /XF "* (r).*" /XD "* (r)*"

...but that does not solve the problem of the "perhaps", the already backed up file...

If I rename manually the "perhaps" to "perhaps (r)", I finally get both of them in my \\test folder, due to the backup loop.

I want to rename the backup version of any (r) BEFORE I call robocopy. It's an ok tweak for me.

I tried the rename command but I can't target the file of another path. I tried to copy and delete, but I'm blocked by the need of doing at least two commands with the same argument, which is something I do not know how to do.

I feel like I should use a "for" somewhere to scan the strings of the files and folders name, but I can't figure out how.

Any advice or help please?

EDIT: here is what I have done, I finaly got 2 files:

sync.bat:

@echo off

echo Sync4.bat
set dest=%UserProfile%\Desktop
echo dest %dest%
echo cd %CD%

for %%I in (.) do if not "%%~nxI" == "" (set "CurrDirName=%%~nxI") else set "CurDirName=\"
echo %CurrDirName%

if EXIST "P:\%CurrDirName%\SyncPURGE.bat" (goto existB)

robocopy /s /xo /dst "%CD%" "%dest%\%CurrDirName%"
robocopy /s /xo /dst "%CD%" "P:\%CurrDirName%"
robocopy /s /xo /dst "%dest%\%CurrDirName%" "%CD%"
robocopy /s /xo /dst "P:\%CurrDirName%" "%CD%"

echo done
timeout 2
goto :eos

:existB
color 0c
echo exec PURGE from the external drive
timeout 5
CD /D P:\%CurrDirName%
call syncPURGE.bat
goto :eos

syncPURGE.bat:

@echo off

color 0c
echo syncPURGE.bat
set dest=%UserProfile%\Desktop
echo dest %dest%
echo cd %CD%

for %%I in (.) do if not "%%~nxI" == "" (set "CurrDirName=%%~nxI") else set "CurDirName=\"
echo %CurrDirName%

robocopy /s /xo /dst /MIR "%CD%" "%dest%\%CurrDirName%"
robocopy /s /xo /dst /MIR "%CD%" "P:\%CurrDirName%"
robocopy /s /xo /dst /MIR "%dest%\%CurrDirName%" "%CD%"
robocopy /s /xo /dst /MIR "P:\%CurrDirName%" "%CD%"

echo PURGE done
timeout 2
del %dest%\%CurrDirName%\SyncPURGE.bat

The /MIR parameter of the syncPURGE.bat batch file deletes any file or directory that has been removed or renamed from the drive where the .bat is executed from.

I mostly keep the sync.bat I'm used to use because it can be launched from the computer or the HDD drive without delete any files or folder (that is useful since I am not always sure of which version is the newer one).

And I can carefully use the syncPURGE.bat when I need to save a modified setup (renamed, deleted or moved files)

As I use multiple computers but only one HDD, I keep the SyncPURGE.bat only on the HDD side.

When I need to change the setup, I copy the SyncPURGE.bat to the computer repository and launch it.

It look like usable thank you, I'll try this setup for a week

items.title: "Extending" consequences to deal with ongoing behaviour
items.human_voice:
So my 10 yo is having self control issues, primarily to do with stealing (limited to treats, drinks etc) that do not belong to him, or controlling his own environment regardless of the effect it has on others.

We have spoken to him about this behaviour, explaining from several different angles:

Perspective of this behaviour happening to him instead; how would he feel if someone had taken something from him? Lollies he got from a party bag, or a drink he bought with his own money?
Self-control is an active thought process; a decision to act one way or another. He has expressed an understanding of this, and has also explained that he is aware of the cause and effect of his behaviour during the action, but still decides to carry out the behaviour.
Financial cost/reimbursement of the behaviours. He earns pocket money with jobs, and putting it simply, again form a different perspective is basically just giving that hard-earned money to someone else. He works for the money, only to have it taken from him.
This also applies to controlling his environment (he turns on lights overnight as a "night light" - he does already have a night light in his room - in his room, in the hallway, and on the front porch outside his bedroom window when he can't sleep). This behaviour costs money, and if it continues (which it has) he will need to do extra work to compensate for the additional incurred costs. We have even pushed the potential of security risks of this, with little apparent impact.

Our latest attempt to explain this (which we use for everyone in the house, including my partner and I) is the "Three C's: Communication, Consideration, and Cooperation" which basically boils down to: we talk to each other when there is conflict, expressing our feelings and what the problem(s) are; we consider each other's feelings; and we find a way to cooperate with each other.

These behaviours have been ongoing for over 6 months, and when we believe there is an improvement in the behaviour, he gets caught out again (either by getting caught red-handed, or new food wrappers/hidden cups in his bedroom during a big clean).

We have decided to give him a consequence of breaking up sticks/branches in the backyard, as well as restrictions to his time on iPads, watching TV etc, and does not get "special treats" unless we say so. He spends an hour each day in the yard, and we have explained that the duration of the punishment is up to him - the more work he does each time, the shorter the duration of the consequence. We allow him to do as he wishes however. If he chooses to simply sit around, that's his decision, though we do remind him of the obligation, and we do supervise to ensure he isn't doing anything he shouldn't be.

However, he is still carrying out the misbehaviour. It is even becoming more frequent, and he does seem unperturbed by the consequences. We have stated that for each time this occurs, he will be adding an additional day to the consequence, but again, this seems to be having little impact. In truth, I believe that this may be becoming an attention seeking behaviour.

His older brother that has different privileges (he has a laptop as a requirement for school) which he uses to play Minecraft with friends, and a phone to contact them. He also has different behaviours (he has invested in Warhammer miniatures, therefore he has a better interest in carrying out his jobs to earn pocket money) however he is also more introverted, but with changes in his social environments, as well as potential early teenage hormonal changes (he is only 12 so this may not be a factor) he has random, violent and emotional outbursts.

He, on the other hand, is still only interested in Lego, and due to his excessive extroverted personality and behaviours (children in his class have expressed that he is "very intense"), he can be very attention seeking, and due to the fact that he doesn't have many people in his life to spend time with, this falls on his mother and I, and his older brother; which does quickly become overbearing.

I am starting to believe that "more consequences, more pressure, more strictness" is not going to work, as I have explained that this is potentially becoming an attention-seeking behaviour, but the original approach of explanation has made no impact either. What can we do to help him correct his behaviours, without causing further conflict within the family?

Some clarifications:

How much attention is he getting? As both of us work a 40-hour week, during this time it is mostly from his older brother (which, as I explained has been directed away from the younger brother to his friends), and his mother and I are generally either spending our own time relaxing, or dealing with cooking, cleaning etc. When it comes to chores, I tend to hover about and keep them both on task, giving compliments and encouragement where I can, particularly if tension is getting high from emotions, stress etc. During the weekends, Mum tries to come up with family activities, like going to the park or visiting family, and we often ask the older brother to spend time away from his devices to do things with us/his brother.

I do believe that due to his intensity - he often "contributes" to a lot of conversations that he is not a part of, or he continues a joke to the point of annoyance, or he jumps to very dark imagery as "funny", probably due to scary/horror games (E.g. Five nights at Freddy's) being a fun topic. This causes us to ask him to stop a lot of the time, or calm down, etc.

In regards to assistance, I am going to personal therapy, my partner has been in and out of therapy for herself, and we are looking into the boy's mental health as well. We have a potential that he may be brushing the spectrum, but we have yet to receive confirmation after an initial analysis. Both boys have been seeing counsellors which has been revealing for us (for example other kids seeing him as being too intense).
What are the major sources of conflict? Primarily emotions - what is "fair" and "unfair" from different perspectives. For example, after several instances of pointing out that a job has not been completed properly, explaining what needs to be done, how it was not achieved, and giving advice on how to do it, make it easy, etc., placing down a consequence for repeated lack of effort is immediately responded with "not fair" which can quickly escalate, especially on stressful days as management of this almost always falls back on me depending on how stressful the day has been for my partner.

In this instance, the only idea of "correcting behaviour" would be to remove any kind of "treat" from the house. However this could end in two ways - everyone feeling this is unfair, "why should everyone suffer because of one person", which would likely punish him indirectly and even harder; or after a stint of inaccessibility, similar to the addiction conundrum of exposure to it causing the initial problem to escalate.

items.title: Should I bother trying to teach my niece I won't respond to tantrums if I only see her once a month and risk her mom undermining me if I don't give in
items.human_voice:
I get to see my niece roughly once a month. Her mother, who is raising her, is not related to me, but we get along well enough. Unfortunately the mother allows her daughter to get away with throwing tantrums to get what she wants. My niece is generally a good kid usually and often cooperates with me, it's kind of random when she will happily go along with something and when a tantrum will happen.

Now I have plenty of experience with different kids, and have dealt with tantrums before. I know how to handle tantrums and express to a child that I love them - even when they are throwing tantrums - but that I also won't give in to a tantrums when I'm officially in charge, I have plenty of practice with that. My problem is that the mother is usually near by during my visits and will show up when she hears her daughter crying. After that the daughter usually ends up getting what she wanted from Mom, meaning her tantrum still ended up working!

To give an idea of frequency I spent half a day with her on Sunday and had to deal with two tantrums in that time. In both cases I refused to give in, in one case Mom came to comfort my niece in the middle of the tantrum rewarding her fighting with extra attention. The other time I just barely managed to get her to say sorry - I'd refused to continue our game until she apologized to her cousin which triggered the tantrum - but only by partially playing dumb with mom as to the cause of the tantrum, distracting Mom for a minute, and dumb luck that niece was just at the state where she was ready to reengage and thankfully didn't decide to keep fighting saying sorry when I asked for it a second time. I felt like I was walking a tightrope trying to get a simple sorry out of my niece now that mom was around.

I know kids can understand different adults have different rules, but if mom is usually close enough to come in and reward the tantrum when I refuse to I'm not sure my niece will learn she shouldn't try tantrums with me; after all tantrums still work via summoning mom. Can a 4 year old really be expected to learn and remember that I won't support tantrums if she sees me only once a month and my attempt to teach her are often interrupted by mom?

I know how to handle tantrums with kids I only volunteer with and won't see regularly as well, I could better distract and defuse such a situation if I wasn't actively trying to teach my niece that she shouldn't try to use tantrums to get things out of me. So I'm torn between using tantrums as a teaching moment to show her that they won't work - which is what I'd prefer to do if it wasn't for my concern it won't work if mom is around- and giving up on teaching and simply resorting to defusing the situation as easily as I can (without fully giving in to the tantrum, I simple refuse to do that), so I can get back to having fun with her and making the most of my visits.

Before anyone suggests it, mom is not open to parenting advice from me. Talking with her about my concerns won't fix things, and could potentially risk alienating her and making it harder to get visits with my niece so it's not really something I want to risk.

items.title: What is a reasonable solution to screen-time evasion?
items.human_voice:
I really didn't expect this outcome. I expected "one hour of screen-time" to mean just that. The child learns to moderate the time spent on an iOS smartphone over waking hours.

In practice the child quickly uses up the hour of screen-time, and then continues indefinitely using the iPhone.

It turns out that there is a loophole. "One more minute" is available in each app. I have yet to figure out how it's used. It's not the case, for example, that an additional minute can be obtained for the same app, but perhaps it's possible to flip-flop between a pair of apps (games), or it's possible to uninstall then reinstall the same app.

That a child is willing to go through that much trouble to evade screen-time is by itself puzzling.

What is a reasonable solution to screen-time evasion?

I'm contemplating:

withdrawing iOS and providing a dumb phone (and dealing with the child's wrath, plus endless comparisons with peers);
replacing iOS with Android, which doesn't seem to have this loophole (oddly, this is more expensive, because of the ability to recycle a gently used device but one with otherwise good specs); or
somehow convincing the child to abandon what starts to look like an addiction.

Have you been there? Did you find a good solution?

Note 1
What the operating system provides can quickly change. I have been having this problem with iOS releases up to and including iOS 17.

Note 2
iOS has an an additional constraint to refuse access during bedtime. Yet one additional setting enables one or more apps to be used regardless of the bedtime or screen-time constraints — notably to be able to call or send a message (seeking help, a ride, etc — the primary function for having a phone in the first place). Neither of these directly solves the main problem described above.

Note 3
(Added after BenjyTec's answer.)
I had already enabled "Block at Downtime" and "Block at End of Limit". They do not help.

items.title: 1.5 year old afraid of everything after an accident
items.human_voice:
I had an accident with my 1.5 year old daughter two days ago: I carried her in my carrier on the chest and, while trying to move a bulky item through a narrow opening, I stumbled so that she was tilted towards the side and hit her head quite hard on an iron gate next to us. She cried and I tried to comfort her immediately. She did not cry for long, less than 5 minutes, and for the rest of the day I did not notice anything strange. We went to bed. In the night, she woke up very often, crying, so at some point I took her into my bed. In the early morning of yesterday, everything seemed still well and normal.

But then we went outside to run errands and there it started: She looked mostly down while walking, which is an unusual behaviour for her. Then she stopped and pointed at the ants on the ground. I told her some things about the ants, we watched them, and then I tried to make her come with me. She did not want to, she seemed troubled. Then a fire bug (much larger than an ant) walked towards her and she started crying and tried to move her feet upwards (yes, both) so that it was clear to me that she was afraid of that bug. So I took her into my arms. Tried to tell her some interesting things about fire bugs, pointed at them, moved a little closer, but she had enough and just wanted to be away from it. Okay, I carried her the rest of the way. Whenever I had to put her down (to get stuff out of my pocket etc.), she looked down and seemed to be scanning for dangers on the ground.

Next issue: After the afternoon nap we went outside to go to the playground. She wanted to walk down the stairs on her own, as usual. Again, she looked down, scanning for dangers. Then she found one: a pebble stone on the stair. She refused to walk any further. She tried going around it, but failed (there was no handrail on the other side so she could not take the step) and just stood there. I tried to show her how interesting that pebble stone was, touched it, walked on it, showed here that it is not dangerous. Didn't help. So I carried her again until outside.

On the playground she accepted all the suggestions I gave her (things she usually likes or loves, like "Do you want to swing?", "Let's bake a sand cake!"), but she was not fully there. I mean mentally. She was absent somehow and could not really enjoy it. In the sand I noticed that she tried to get rid of every bit of sand on her hands all the time.

During dinner, she was mostly normal again (we found something to make her laugh again before dinner, so her mood seemed to be good), but like in the sand, whenever she spilled something (even if just a little drop of tea or a bread crumb), she wanted it cleaned.

The night I let her sleep with me from the beginning. She cried often in the night, but did not seem to wake up (just some cries, then silence again, eyes closed all the time).

Today I went to the doctor with her to have a look at the bump on her head. Was afraid that I damaged something. But the doctor said they have no reason to believe that there is any long-term physical damage (like bone fracture or brain damage): She did not vomit, she did not pass out, she did not behave lethargic for almost 48 hours after the accident. Her pupils and reflexes are all normal, and the bump is not very large.

So let's assume the strange behaviour is "merely" psychological. I can imagine that the incident is/was very hard on her psychologically: She was in the most comfortable, most secure/safe situation she knows (carried by me in the carrier). And then she got hit so hard out of nothing. She could not even see anything coming because her face was towards me, she was hit on the back of her head. I know that such things - experiencing something unexpected and painful in a situation that is associated with complete security/safety - can destroy confidence in life, at least for adults. So why not for children as well?

So I just have one question: What can I do to help her get over it?

At her age, she has not enough verbal skills to understand me if I explain to her what happened.

I have to note that I myself had an anxiety disorder as a child (started around age 10, slowly faded away around 18), and that increased need for order and cleanliness (like with the sand on her hands and spilled food during dinner) is a clear sign of stress in my case. So she may have gotten all the ingredients, genetically, to develop an anxiety disorder herself.

items.title: nvim overseer.nvim でtmuxを使ってる環境でペインを縦分割している状態で下画面の横幅全体に表示させる方法
items.human_voice:
質問内容
タイトル通りなのですが、tmuxを使ってる環境でペインを縦分割している状況で、行いたい画面構成の画像のように

下に幅いっぱいでタスクランナーを表示したいのですが、tmuxを使っている関係で実行したときのペインの幅いっぱいにしか表示されず。物理ウインドウ自体の幅いっぱいに描画させる方法がわかりません。

起きている問題
実行したときの現在のペインの幅いっぱいにしか表示されない

実装したいこと
行いたい画面構成のように物理ウインドウの下に幅いっぱいにペインを跨いで全体に描画する方法が知りたい

ついでですが、経過時間の時刻も非表示にしたい

前提
Tmuxを使っているのtmux前提

調べたこと
tmuxでCtrl + b "で横分割して、 Ctrl + b <space>でを何度か押して提示画像のような状態になることを確認

gemini,chatGPTなどで調べて色々設定ファルを編集

提示コード

------------------------------------------------------------------
--- Love2D Commands
------------------------------------------------------------------

-- F5キーで親方向から main.lua を探し、安全に LÖVE を実行＋Overseerを開く
vim.keymap.set("n", "<F5>", function()
-- 現在開いているファイルの場所、またはカレントディレクトリを起点にする
local current_file = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(0)
local start_path = current_file ~= "" and vim.fs.dirname(current_file) or vim.fn.getcwd()

-- 上方向（upward）に main.lua を検索
local match = vim.fs.find("main.lua", {
path = start_path,
upward = true,
stop = vim.loop.os_homedir(),
limit = 1,
})

-- main.lua が見つかった場合
if match[1] then
local love_dir = vim.fs.dirname(match[1])
local overseer = require("overseer")

-- 古いログバッファが残っていれば削除
if love_terminal_buf and vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(love_terminal_buf) then
vim.api.nvim_buf_delete(love_terminal_buf, { force = true })
end

overseer.strategy = {
"toggleterm",
---"tmux",
---"terminal",

use_terminal = true,
direction = "current",
quit_on_exit = "never",
}

-- 古いログバッファが残っていれば削除
if love_terminal_buf and vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(love_terminal_buf) then
vim.api.nvim_buf_delete(love_terminal_buf, { force = true })
end

local current_win = vim.api.nvim_get_current_win()

local task = overseer.new_task({
cmd = { "love", love_dir },
name = "Run LÖVE (" .. vim.fs.basename(love_dir) .. ")",
-- 作成した最下部ペイン（current）に標準ターミナルとしてログを流し込む

})

vim.cmd("OverseerOpen")
task:start()
-- vim.cmd("botright split")
-- vim.cmd("resize 12") -- ペインの高さ（行数）

-- 3. 安全にバッファIDを記憶する（OverseerのAPIに依存しない）
vim.defer_fn(function()
if vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(current_win) then
-- 今開いているペインのバッファIDを直接取得
love_terminal_buf = vim.api.nvim_win_get_buf(current_win)

-- ゲーム終了後も勝手にペインが閉じないように、バッファを維持する
if vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(love_terminal_buf) then
vim.bo[love_terminal_buf].bufhidden = "hide"
end
end
end, 50)

else
vim.notify("main.lua が見つかりませんでした！", vim.log.levels.ERROR, { title = "LÖVE Run Error" })
end
end,{ desc = "Find main.lua and run LÖVE safely" })

items.title: Llamada a un procedure sobre cargado dentro de un procedure en un paquete de Oracle/PLSQL
items.human_voice:
Tengo una duda sobre este paquete:

create or replace PACKAGE BODY emp_pkg IS

FUNCTION valid_deptid(p_deptid IN departments.department_id%TYPE)
RETURN BOOLEAN IS
v_dummy PLS_INTEGER;
BEGIN
SELECT 1
INTO v_dummy
FROM departments
WHERE department_id = p_deptid;

RETURN TRUE;
EXCEPTION
WHEN NO_DATA_FOUND THEN
RETURN FALSE;
END valid_deptid;

PROCEDURE add_employee( **----PRIMER PROCEDURE**
p_first_name employees.first_name%TYPE,
p_last_name employees.last_name%TYPE,
p_email employees.email%TYPE,
p_job employees.job_id%TYPE DEFAULT 'SA_REP',
p_mgr employees.manager_id%TYPE DEFAULT 145,
p_sal employees.salary%TYPE DEFAULT 1000,
p_comm employees.commission_pct%TYPE DEFAULT 0,
p_deptid employees.department_id%TYPE DEFAULT 30) IS
BEGIN
IF valid_deptid(p_deptid) THEN
INSERT INTO employees(employee_id, first_name, last_name,
email, job_id, manager_id, hire_date, salary, commission_pct,
department_id)
VALUES (employees_seq.NEXTVAL, p_first_name, p_last_name,
p_email, p_job, p_mgr, TRUNC(SYSDATE), p_sal, p_comm, p_deptid);
ELSE
RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR(-20204, 'Invalid department ID.');
END IF;
END add_employee;

PROCEDURE add_employee ( **---- SEGUNDO PROCEDURE, SOBRECARGADO**
p_first_name employees.first_name%TYPE,
p_last_name employees.last_name%TYPE,
p_deptid employees.department_id%TYPE) IS
p_email employees.email%TYPE;
BEGIN
p_email := UPPER(SUBSTR(p_first_name, 1, 1)||SUBSTR(p_last_name, 1, 7));
add_employee(p_first_name, p_last_name, p_email, p_deptid => p_deptid);
END;

PROCEDURE get_employee(
p_empid IN employees.employee_id%TYPE,
p_sal OUT employees.salary%TYPE,
p_job OUT employees.job_id%TYPE) IS
BEGIN
SELECT salary, job_id
INTO p_sal, p_job
FROM employees
WHERE employee_id = p_empid;

END get_employee;

END emp_pkg;

Lo primero a decir es que este código FUNCIONA pero no entiendo un aspecto de su estructura y es el siguiente: en el procedure sobrecargado (el que tiene tres parámetros) se hace una llamada al primer procedure (que tiene 8 parámetros):

add_employee(p_first_name, p_last_name, p_email, p_deptid => p_deptid);

Comportamiento

===============

--Los primeros parámetros de la llamada (p_first_name, p_last_name) son los primeros parámetros del primer procedure, que son llamados de manera posicional. Hasta ahí todo claro.

--Después, el p_email NO ES el tercer parámetro del primer procedure, es la variable local (también llamada p_email) del segundo procedure.

--Y para finalizar, después de omitir los parámetros que son DEFAULT, se pone p_deptid => p_deptid, siendo el primero un parámetro formal del primer procedure y el otro un parámetro actual del segundo procedure.

===============

*DUDA 1: ¿Por qué Oracle identifica p_email con la variable local del segundo procedure cuando tiene el mismo nombre que el tercer parámetro del primer procedure? ¿No lo tendría que identificar con el tercer parámetro del primer procedure ya que lo estamos llamando? Lo he cambiado por v_email para distinguirlo y funciona igual.

*DUDA 2:
¿Se pueden mezclar parámetros del primer procedure junto a variables locales del segundo procedure sobrecargado (el de tres parámetros) dentro de una llamada?

*DUDA 3:
¿Por qué es necesario hacer p_deptid => p_deptid y asignar un parámetro actual? ¿Al ver Oracle el parámetro p_deptid aislado no lo identificaría con el p_deptid del primer procedure?

items.title: How do I raise concerns about workload and pay without throwing a poorly performing colleague under the bus
items.human_voice:
I work remotely for a small IT company with around 20 employees. The development team consists of roughly ten mostly mid-to-senior developers, one junior developer and several testers. We meet in person about twice a year.

I joined less than 12 months ago and have become one of the more productive members of the team. I have taken on some fairly complex work and introduced changes that reduced our reliance on expensive third-party APIs, resulting in meaningful cost savings.
My annual review is coming up, and I already feel that my experience, output and impact justify a pay rise. However, there is another issue that is beginning to affect my motivation.

One developer has been with the company for at least five or six years but consistently produces very little work, and what he does produce is often of a poor standard. He is regularly assigned simple BAU tickets that another developer could complete in 10-15 minutes, but he may spend most of a day on them and then require another day to address basic code review feedback.

Because he completes lots of small tickets, his output might look reasonable to someone who does not understand their complexity. In reality, even our junior developer appears to produce considerably more useful work, despite presumably being paid much less.
When this developer receives anything moderately difficult, he will often get stuck and ask someone else to guide him through most of the solution over a video call. When I first joined, I was happy to help because I wanted to support the team and demonstrate that I was collaborative. Over time, it has started to feel less like mentoring and more like completing his work for him, particularly as he often seems to have made little effort to investigate the problem himself.

A recent PR made the problem particularly obvious. It contained completely irrelevant emoji-related code, apparently generated by an AI coding tool. The ticket had nothing to do with emojis, so it was clear that the output had barely been reviewed or tested before the PR was opened.

The difficult part is that he is genuinely a nice person. We get on well outside the day-to-day work, and I do not want to damage that relationship or make this personal. My concern is entirely about his contribution as a teammate.

The company has a relatively flat structure, and although I have not seen anyone else's salary, I suspect we earn roughly the same amount despite the difference in experience, responsibility and output. That is increasingly making me question why I am pushing myself so hard while somebody else can contribute very little without any apparent consequences.

Our CEO is approachable but primarily sales-focused and does not get involved much in project management. The project manager handles ticket allocation and gets on particularly well with this developer. I like and respect the PM, but it seems clear that the weaker developer is deliberately given simple work while more capable developers are repeatedly assigned the difficult tasks.

This does not appear to be temporary. I have looked through several years of his previous PRs, and the same pattern seems to have existed from the beginning.

As far as I can tell, nobody has formally raised his performance with management. The company has a very relaxed culture, with limited performance management or accountability, so problems like this appear to be tolerated rather than addressed.

There sometimes seems to be little incentive for people to challenge poor performance, provided everyone continues completing enough work to keep things moving. This may explain why the situation has continued for several years without intervention.

For my annual review, I intend to focus on my own results, responsibilities and the value I have delivered rather than directly comparing myself with another employee. However, the unequal workload and the expectation that stronger developers will compensate for weaker ones are starting to become a genuine concern.
How should I approach this?

Should I raise the wider workload problem during my review, or keep the discussion strictly focused on my own performance and salary?

Also, how can I set reasonable boundaries when he asks me to effectively complete difficult tickets for him without becoming unhelpful or damaging our working relationship?

Constructive advice would be appreciated.

items.title: I'm going back to coding by hand
items.human_voice: I have a successful app I built myself with a solid user base. I had been working on a new version via Claude on and off for about six monthsIn work we use LLMs exclusively. Nobody writes code anymore. It's all hands off and we have a high level understanding of how things work but no more than that.When it comes to my side project, I was adding features at breakneck speed with Claude but I realized I have no clue how the new code works or what it changes or breaks. I spent many years of my life working on this project and I don't want to turn it into another vibe coded black box, especially without an org of other engineers to help.So last night, I abandoned my Claude branch with all the fancy new things and started hand coding again.It was very very satisfying. Sure, there was monotony. I changed some variable names and I had to chase down all the places they were referenced, comment out tons of stuff to get things working and then slowly bring it back in, but it felt like coming home to an untidy house after living in hotels for half a year, and starting to clean up. Yeah there's work to do, but this place is mine. My own. I know where things live.It's given me love and energy for the project again (at least for now, I hope it continues!) and I'm delighted to say I took a good look at code I myself had written pre Claude and I still found many ways to write it better, refactor, make it more readable and efficient. I haven't forgotten.If anyone is feeling the despair of not coding anymore, stairs you're losing your edge, I would suggest you ditch Claude for a few days at least and see how you feel. Your mileage may vary, but it's given me back something I thought was gone forever

items.title: グリッド状に取得した大量顕微鏡画像（約1700枚）のツギハギで累積ズレ（ドリフト）を抑える方法（Python / OpenCV）
items.human_voice:
Python（OpenCV / NumPy）で、約1700枚の顕微鏡画像を1枚の画像へと合体（モザイク合成）させようとしています。

しかし画像上で重なるべき所でうまく重ならなかったり、意図しない黒い線が入ったりする問題を解決できずに困っています。

【背景】

テストベッドの上に微粒子が載っており、この粒子こそが被写体です。

テストベッドの隅から顕微鏡を等間隔に移動させ、これらの粒子を撮影していきます。

撮影された画像同士全てをくっつけて、一つの画像にしようとしています。

各画像のファイル名には撮影時のステージ位置が含まれており、例えば以下のような形式です：

00000_00000.jpg

00000_00030.jpg

00030_00000.jpg

この数値は2方向の移動量（0.1 mm単位）を表しており、画像はグリッド状に取得されています。

現在扱っている画像は横方向に3mmずつ、縦方向にも3mmずつ移動して撮影されました。

3ｍｍでは画像名は00030といったものになります。1ｍｍでは00010

以下の図はその撮影時のイメージです。

図1　撮影の概要図

現在の処理は以下の通りです：

校正用画像から pixels_per_mm を取得
ファイル名の座標 → mm → pixel に変換
グリッド状に配置
np.maximum を用いて重ね合わせ

簡略化すると次のようなコードです。実際のコードは650行程度のものになります：

pos_x = col_index * step_x_px
pos_y = row_index * step_y_px

canvas[y:y+h, x:x+w] = np.maximum(canvas[y:y+h, x:x+w], img)

この方法で大まかな位置は維持できているのですが、以下の問題があります：

・わずかな位置ズレが全体で累積し、ドリフトが発生する

・画像境界に黒線や継ぎ目が現れる

今回の画像は顕微鏡で取得した粒子（または表面）画像で、

テクスチャが少なく、隣接画像間で非常に似たパターンが繰り返されています。

そのため、

・SIFT / ORB などの特徴点ベース手法は安定しない

・全画像に対する重い画像レジストレーションは避けたい

という前提があります。

目的は以下です：

・グリッド配置をベースに維持する

・小さなズレのみを補正する

・黒線の抑制よりも位置ズレの抑制を優先する（とはいえ黒線は無い方がよい。）

合体した画像の例と、解決したい問題である画像のズレ、「黒線」を図2に示します

図2　貼り合わせの実例、黒線、解決したい問題

質問です：

・今回のようなグリッド状の画像貼り合わで、ズレを抑える良い方法はありますか？

・隣接画像同士で軽量にズレを推定する方法（例：位相相関など）は有効でしょうか？

このような「ステージ位置ベースの大量画像合成」でよく使われる手法があれば教えてください。

できるだけ軽量で安定した方法を用いて現在発生している問題を解決したいと考えています。

よろしくお願いいたします。

TLS is Let's Encrypt and SSL Labs gives it an A+.

So far I've fixed a broken AAAA record and a missing IPv6 default route. I've also ruled out NAT64/IPv6 and TLS/ATS compatibility issues.

The interesting thing is that this is only happening to a small number of US users and across different iOS versions.

Right now I'm wondering if this could be related to stale keep-alive connections and carrier NAT/network changes.

I've currently changed:

keepalive_timeout 15s;
ssl_session_tickets off;

and also fixed a Connection: upgrade header issue.

I'm monitoring it now to see if the errors stop.

Has anyone run into bad record mac + while keepalive like this, particularly with iOS users on cellular networks? I'm interested in any other possible causes I should check.

session = requests.Session()
session.headers.update({

items.title: How can I deescalate a conversation with a close friend when misunderstandings keep building up?
items.human_voice:
I recently had an argument over text with a close friend. We don’t argue often, but when we do, it sometimes can escalate quickly.

This time, the argument started when I misinterpreted one of their comments about my choice to consult a professional for something, instead of figuring it out on my own. (A couple weeks prior, I had also asked them for some advice.) Now, I explained my rationale and thought that I was making the right decision for myself, so their wording struck me as dismissive:

I personally would just go by trial and error, but you do you.

It felt a little ridiculing, and I had trouble finding words to continue the conversation, so I went a little quiet for a few minutes before letting them know I was going to bed and wished them a good evening. I quickly calmed down and realized I had overreacted, but they had already messaged me to say they noticed my quietness, and guessed that I was upset about their comment. I apologized for my overreaction, and I said that they shouldn't worry about it too much.

They shared more on their perspective to explain why they made that comment, and I told them I understood their point and appreciated their honest thoughts and advice. They added another comment which didn't entirely sit right with me:

Anyways, I don't know how much this info is worth, cause you first said you'd like tips and then got mad when I said I would personally just figure it out myself instead of paying someone else.

I then followed up with:

I don't mean to draw this out too much, I do want to be honest with you though. I think it's a little unfair to write that I simply just got mad. I did ask for your advice before and you shared some, which I really appreciated. However, I can't really agree that simply saying you'd do trial and error, is a helpful piece of advice without explanation. You just shared your whole rationale on that here which is much appreciated and it makes sense. But in the moment you just said that one line and that wasn't really constructive.

After that, the conversation quickly began to spiral. They explicitly stated that they were upset over my response, and they felt that I was labeling all of their advice as unconstructive. They also felt that my above response was "very blown out of proportion" and that I was attacking them. As I continued to try and clarify my intentions, they told me:

This honestly makes me less likely to want to ever give tips or advice in the future.

They repeatedly expressed that they felt unappreciated. I tried to reassure them and clarify that I genuinely valued their input, but each clarification seemed to make them more defensive and I felt like my words were not getting through the way I intended. Things continued to take turns for the worse over the span of multiple hours. I constantly felt like I was trying to apologize for and clear up misunderstandings, while attempting to validate their effort in helping me.

Eventually, they started bringing up past disagreements, including a comment about how they felt they had to always tread carefully whenever giving me advice and that it's an uncomfortable environment. The conversation became emotionally draining for both of us, as I then started feeling more upset by some of their language, and communicated that to them. We both acknowledged that it should have not escalated to that point, but it seemed like for a while we just weren't getting through to each other. Although we finally concluded the conversation on a somewhat decent note, I have been left feeling like I was pulled into these deep layers of misunderstandings and couldn't deescalate, despite my conscious efforts to maintain respectful communication.

In future situations like this, how can I most effectively break out of a defensive cycle once it’s started, and clarify my perspective without making my friend feel attacked?

For what it's worth -

I tend to prefer verbal communication when it comes to serious conversations like this, but it's not always possible between us due to availability. I did try to bring this conversation into a call at one point, but decided to continue over text.
We never used blatantly inflammatory or disrespectful language when talking to each other.
The last time we had an argument like this was a couple years ago, and they felt that they needed some space between us for a couple months before we slowly reconnected.
I consider this person to be one of my most cherished friends and we spend a lot of time together.

items.title: lua言語でスクリプト言語を活かした迅速なゲーム開発するには？
items.human_voice:
質問内容
タイトル通り、Love2D（Lua言語）を使って2Dゲームを作っているのですが、C++との思想の違いや設計の落とし込み方に困っています。

知りたいこと
Lua特有の「テーブル」という仕組みを活かした、スクリプト言語らしい実装方法やコーディング手法（設計パターン）を知りたいです。

調べたこと、考えたこと

C++と違って構造体やクラスが存在せず、すべてを「テーブル」で表現するため、現状は1つのファイルを1つのクラスに見立ててメンバ関数などをすべて書いている状態です。

たとえば function Deck.get_card() 内で（C系ではアンチパターンとされるような）無限ループを記述してしまったり、function Card.new(number,suit,quad) でクラスのインスタンス生成を模倣したりと、結果的に「C++の書き方をそのままスクリプト言語で再現している」状態になってしまっています。

コミュニティ等で調べると「Luaは何をやっても自由（自由度が高い）」と言われます。

Luaではあらゆるデータ構造をテーブルとして扱うこと自体は理解しています。

現状
スクリプト言語の良さを活かせず、C/C++の設計を無理やり再現したようなコード設計になっています。

前提

作っているもの：トランプゲーム（ポーカーの役を作るだけのシンプルなゲーム）

提示コードについて
一部ですが、カード（Card）、デッキ（Deck）、メイン関数（main）のコードを掲載します。

設計や書き方について添削・アドバイスをお願いします。

Deck.lua
local Card = require("card")

local Deck = {}

love.graphics.setDefaultFilter("nearest", "nearest")

-- Initialize the deck
Deck.indexCards = {} -- Index of cards
Deck.usedCards = {} -- Used of cards
Deck.cards = {} -- rest of cards

function Deck.Init()

-- Create a standard deck of 52 cards
local suits = {"physics", "magic"}

for _, suit in ipairs(suits) do
for number = 0, 6 do

local card = nil
if(suit == "physics") then

card = Card.new(number + 1, suit, love.graphics.newQuad(number * Card.width,0,Card.width,Card.height,Card.sprite))

elseif(suit == "magic") then
card = Card.new(number + 1, suit, love.graphics.newQuad(number * Card.width,Card.height,Card.width,Card.height,Card.sprite))
end

table.insert(Deck.indexCards, card)
table.insert(Deck.usedCards, card)
table.insert(Deck.cards, card)

end
end

end

function Deck.get_card()

if #Deck.cards == 0 then
print("No more cards in the deck!")
return nil
end

-- Draw a random card from the deck

local card = nil

-- random get a card from cards
while(true) do

local index = love.math.random(1, #Deck.cards)
card = Deck.cards[index]

if card.canUse then
card.canUse = false -- Mark the card as used
card = Deck.cards[index]
break
end
end

card.isActive = true -- Mark the card as active
--print(card)
return card
end

return Deck

Main.lua

local World = require("world")

local Camera = require("camera")

local Mouse = require("mouse")
local Deck = require("deck")

local Player = require("player")

-- Base window size
local BASE_WINDOW_WIDTH = 2560
local BASE_WINDOW_HEIGHT = 1440

-- Current window size
local windowWidth = BASE_WINDOW_WIDTH
local windowHeight = BASE_WINDOW_HEIGHT

local scale = {x = 1, y = 1}
local font = nil

-- Conveter from HEX to RGBA
function HEX(hex)
hex = hex:gsub("#", "") -- '#' を削除

local r = tonumber(hex:sub(1, 2), 16) / 255
local g = tonumber(hex:sub(3, 4), 16) / 255
local b = tonumber(hex:sub(5, 6), 16) / 255
local a = #hex >= 8 and (tonumber(hex:sub(7, 8), 16) / 255) or 1

return r, g, b, a
end

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
--- Resize
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function love.resize(w,h)

Camera.update_scale(w, h)
font = love.graphics.newFont(70 * ( (Camera.scale().x + Camera.scale().y) / 2) )
font:setFilter("nearest", "nearest")
love.graphics.setFont(font)
end

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
--- Load
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

function love.load()
World.init()
Camera.init(BASE_WINDOW_WIDTH,BASE_WINDOW_HEIGHT)
Mouse.init()
Deck.Init() -- Init the deck

Player.int() -- Init the player
Player.set_card(1) -- Init the player

-- print(World.body_count())

love.graphics.setDefaultFilter("nearest", "nearest")

font = love.graphics.newFont(70 * ( (Camera.scale().x + Camera.scale().y) / 2) )
love.graphics.setFont(font)

love.graphics.setBackgroundColor(HEX("#008751"))

end

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
--- Update
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function love.update(dt)
World.update(dt)
Mouse.update()
Player.update()
end

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
--- Events
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- ESC to quit
love.keypressed = function(key)
if key == "escape" then
love.event.quit()
end
end

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
--- Draw
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function love.draw()

Mouse.draw()
Player.draw()

Camera.submit()
end

Card.lua
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
--- Card
---
--- 1 card data
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local World = require("world")
local Tween = require("lib.tween.tween")

love.graphics.setDefaultFilter("nearest", "nearest")

local Card = {}

-- 1 card size
Card.width = 16
Card.height = (8 * 3)

Card.sprite = love.graphics.newImage("sprite.png")

Card.__index = Card

function Card.new(number,suit,quad)

local self = setmetatable({},Card)

self.tweenHandle = nil
self.collisionSize = {width = Card.width * 10, height = Card.height * 10}

--print("Card size: " .. Card.width * 10 .. " x " .. Card.height * 10)
self.__index = Card

self.name = "Card: " .. suit .. number
self.position = {x = 500, y = 500}

-- card and suit
self.number = number
self.suit = suit

-- sprite quad
self.quad = quad

-- collision sensor
self.collision = World.create_sensor(0, 0,self.collisionSize.width,self.collisionSize.height, self)
self.collision.isActive = true
-- can
self.canUse = true
return self
end

local function deep_copy(obj)
-- テーブル以外（数値、文字列、ブーリアンなど）はそのまま返す
if type(obj) ~= 'table' then
return obj
end

-- 新しいテーブルを作成し、メタテーブルも引き継ぐ
local copy = setmetatable({}, getmetatable(obj))

-- 内部の要素を再帰的にコピー
for k, v in pairs(obj) do
copy[k] = deep_copy(v)
end

return copy
end

function Card:on_click()
local dy = self.position.y
self.tweenHandle = Tween.new(0.25,self.position,{ y = dy - (self.collisionSize.height * 0.8) }, 'outQuad')

print(self.tweenHandle)
end

function Card:clone()
return deep_copy(self)
end

function Card:update()

if self.tweenHandle then
local complete = self.tweenHandle:update(love.timer.getDelta())
if complete then
self.tweenHandle = nil
end
end

local dx = (self.position.x) + (self.collisionSize.width / 2)
local dy = (self.position.y) + (self.collisionSize.height / 2)

self.collision.body:setPosition(dx,dy)
end

function Card:draw()
love.graphics.draw(Card.sprite,self.quad,self.position.x,self.position.y,0,10,10)
end

return Card

items.title: Dealing with 10-12 yer old impulsiveness
items.human_voice:
I have 2 sons, aged 10 and 12 and lately they have been dealing with a lot of different things.

So far, their uncle died rather suddenly after Christmas, then my dog died (old age), and now the widowed aunt is living with us, during her grieving period.

Amongst all of this, the boys have had issues with impulsiveness. The 10 year old has always had issues with stealing, which has been reduced to lollies, rather than some of the bigger things he used to steal, but is now not going to sleep - we have to force him to stay in bed, play music, turn the lights off, and monitor that he is actually staying in bed.

The 12 year old has recieved a laptop to be used for school, and has managed to steal the WiFi password, (which I am yet to change, though it was already a custom password - he had retrieved it from his iPad) and claims that it simply "automatically connects" whenever he gets caught using it when he shouldn't. We do allow him to use it for an hour or so after school for homework/assessments, but disconnect him afterwards. (I work in IT so I make sure that he shouldn't be able to access it when he is not allowed).

They have however both grown more impulsive - waking up in the middle of the night to connect to the WiFi, or to play video games in the loungeroom.

They both have an iPad, which is again limited to timeframes of when they can it and how long for. They have also connected this behaviour to the recent events, but they refuse to come to us to talk about it, instead calling "kids helpline" in Australia, to express their oppressed situation. But when we approach them, they state that they don't feel comfortable expressing themselves to us.

For reference, we allow them to use their iPads any time after lunch, until bedtime, but restrict certain things such as YouTube, but allow free access to puzzle games (machinarium) or creative apps (duolingo or "blek") or simple games like relaxing fishing games. During school days this is limited to the afternoons only, before the evening processes begin - afternoon chores, dinner, bedtime process.

Video games are limited to an hour (minecraft, mariokart, Super Smash bros), but we do allow extensions on these based on behaviour.

We express an open household, helping each other with chores, rewards for good behaviour (more free time on devices, or treats, etc), consequencesfor bad behaviour, such as temporarily removing access to the focus of the "crime", like devices for the day, etc. Cooperation, consideration of each other, and communication, different methods to do so, expression of feelings, actions and outcomes, trust... as much as we can, even as gentle reminders such as "10 more minutes then turning it off".

When they get caught out doing the wrong thing, and questioned about it, "why are you doing the wrong thing", they simply repeat back what we have discussed in the past, which means they do listen, but they are not following through on their behaviour and actions; self control bring the current and ongoing issue.

This has all been going on and growing over 4 months, and is reaching the point where my partner and I are looking for alternate solutions, beyond simply punishment or different allowances or complete restiction, alternative activities (the younger one loves lego, and skateboarding, which we greatly encourage; the elder one reads quite a lot and has miniatures that he builds and paints, and we have introduced him to a gaming club so he has company with these activities).

items.title: Why are recommended newborn feed volumes much bigger than typical stomach size for the same age?
items.human_voice:
Many sources will tell you the following supposed facts about a newborn baby's biology, or very similar ones:

A newborn's stomach is tiny and it remains quite small for a while. For instance, one source says that by day 10, her stomach is only the size of a golf ball. This is about 40ml.
A baby's stomach cannot stretch.
It takes 1-2 hours for consumed breast milk to leave the stomach, while formula takes twice as long to digest.

(I've included arbitrary links to back up each claim by way of example, but I see claims along these lines everywhere, albeit often with somewhat different numbers.)

Meanwhile, infant formula packaging advises giving a baby of age 0-2 weeks 90ml of formula per feed, and a review of the notes I've kept on my week-old daughter's feeds reveals we gave her a 70ml formula feed on day 6 and an 80ml pumped breast milk feed today, on day 7.

The apparent contradiction is hopefully obvious; the amounts of liquid we are recommended to feed newborns - and that they can observably consume! - are at some ages more than twice as large as the supposed size of their supposedly inelastic stomachs that the fluid will supposedly take over an hour to pass through. This doesn't seem to just be a matter of babies developing at different speeds, either; I'm not (as far as I can tell) comparing a maximum feed volume against a minimum stomach size or anything like that. Instead the typical amounts we're told a newborn should consume are simply much larger than what we're told a newborn's typical stomach size is.

My baby thankfully hasn't exploded, but if everything I've been told about her biology is true, I'm not really sure how that can be the case. Is there something I'm missing about how her body works that resolves the paradox - for instance, after a feed of more milk than her stomach size, does milk/formula somehow wait in the oesophagus until there's space in the stomach? (This isn't how I understand the oesophagus to work.) Or, when she's overfed, does milk get forced out of the end of the stomach undigested? (Then what happens to it next? And is this problematic or at least wasteful?) Or is the contradiction real, and the explanation simply that the claims people make about stomach size aren't true?

items.title: Cómo evitar el error "Target page closed" en Playwright/Browserless al hacer clic en un checkbox?
items.human_voice:
Estoy teniendo un problema con un script de Playwright (en Python) que se ejecuta perfectamente en mi máquina local, pero falla consistentemente cuando se ejecuta en Browserless (conectado vía CDP).

El script falla en un punto muy específico: al hacer clic en un checkbox.

El Contexto:

Ejecución Local (Funciona):

Uso p.chromium.launch(slow_mo=300).

Debido al slow_mo, el script es lento pero logra pasar el clic en el checkbox (aunque falla más adelante por otros motivos).

Ejecución en Browserless (Falla):

Uso p.chromium.connect_over_cdp(...) (sin slow_mo, a máxima velocidad).

El script ejecuta los primeros pasos (login, navegación) sin problema.

Llega al Paso 8, encuentra la fila, e intenta hacer clic en el checkbox.

Inmediatamente después de imprimir "📌 Marcando checkbox...", el script colapsa.

El Error Exacto:

El log muestra que el navegador se cierra justo en la acción de clic:

Fragmento de código

📌 Marcando checkbox...
⚠️ Error checkbox: Target page, context or browser has been closed
Call log:

waiting for locator(...).first
locator resolved to <div ...>
attempting click action
element is visible, enabled and stable
performing click actio... (AQUÍ COLAPSA)

Creo que esto es una medida anti-bot que se activa por la velocidad.

El método .click() de Playwright es instantáneo, sin coordenadas ni movimiento de mouse. Es probable que el servidor (o el propio Browserless) detecte esta acción súper-rápida como no-humana y cierre la sesión para detener el bot.

Mi Pregunta

Para solucionar esto, estoy proponiendo reemplazar el .click() directo:

Python

ANTES (Falla en Browserless)
chkbox.click()

por una simulación de "clic humano" que mueva el cursor y simule un clic físico:

Python

DESPUÉS (Solución propuesta)
box = chkbox.bounding_box()
if box:
# Mover el mouse "hacia" el elemento
page.mouse.move(box["x"] + box["width"] / 2, box["y"] + box["height"] / 2, steps=5)
time.sleep(0.1)
# Clic físico
page.mouse.down()
time.sleep(0.05)
page.mouse.up()
print(" ✅ Checkbox marcado (método humano).")

¿Es esta la forma correcta o estándar de manejar este tipo de detección anti-bot? ¿O existe un método más eficiente en Playwright para parecer "más humano" al interactuar con elementos y evitar que la página se cierre?

items.title: Why doesn't setting "justMyCode": false allow my breakpoint to work?
items.human_voice:
I was debugging some code with an async socket server and found that some breakpoints in the message handler (handle_client) were being ignored. After far too much head scratching I came to realize it was due to a naming conflict. I had named the module socket.py which conflicts with the built-in module of the same name. From what I understand, the default config in VSCode with debugpy is to ignore built-in and imported modules (i.e. "justMyCode": true). I set "justMyCode": false in my launch config and the breakpoints were still being ignored. Even though the debugger thinks this is a built-in module because of the naming conflict shouldn't it now allow the breakpoints?

VSCode 1.136.1
debugpy 2026.6.0

Sample:

#socket.py (breakpoints don't work with this name but work when renamed)
import asyncio

async def run_server():
server = await asyncio.start_server(handle_client, 'localhost', 8888)
addr = server.sockets[0].getsockname()
print(f'Serving on {addr}')
async with server:
await server.serve_forever()

async def handle_client(reader: asyncio.StreamReader, writer: asyncio.StreamWriter):
data = await reader.read(100) ## breakpoints in here were ignored
message = data.decode()
addr = writer.get_extra_info('peername')
print(f"Received {message} from {addr}")
writer.write(f"Hello {message}".encode())
await writer.drain()
writer.close()
await writer.wait_closed()

asyncio.run(run_server())

sample client:

import asyncio

async def send_message(message):
reader, writer = await asyncio.open_connection('localhost', 8888)

writer.write(message.encode())
await writer.drain()

data = await reader.read(100)
response = data.decode()

print(f"Received {response}")

writer.close()
await writer.wait_closed()

asyncio.run(send_message("World"))

items.title: Best messaging pattern for server that spawns multiple workers
items.human_voice:
I'm writing a system in which a server program will spawn multiple worker processes (using CreateProcessA) to work on tasks in parallel. I want to use ZeroMQ to communicate tasks to the workers and communicate progress back to the server. The server will keep track of what worker is working on what task.

My biggest question is what messaging pattern I should use for this kind of communication: router-dealer, router-router, pub-sub, ect.?

As a point of comparison, if I used Win32 named pipes for communication, I could send messages to specific workers using the handle I get from CreateNamedPipe, even if every worker used the same pipe name.

How can I get this behavior with ZeroMQ? I want all workers to send all their messages to the same server, and the server to be able to send messages to specific workers. I don't need broadcasting.

I would like to avoid having the same message sent to multiple peers, as some of the messages can get very large (on the order of several GB).

No projeto frontend (Vue, SCSS, TS) que estou trabalhando hoje há uma cultura relacionada à importação de componentes: não se deve importar os arquivos auxiliares de um componente .vue, somente o componente em si. Isso acontece porque caso haja arquivo de estilo ou lógica que seja compartilhado (e precisaria ser importado em outro lugar), provavelmente isso significa que ele deveria ser ou um componente à parte no próprio módulo, ou um componente do kernel (que atua como se fosse o framework desse projeto), ou, se for a lógica, deveria ser um service. Para todo caso a regra é simples:

De dentro da pasta /components de cada módulo só se pode importar os arquivos .vue, nada mais (os .ts, .scss não). O módulo especial "kernel" é a única exceção.

Como eu disse, isso é "garantido" através da cultura da equipe, mas como o projeto cresceu e a equipe também (em número), gostaria de saber se há alguma forma de fazer isso ser garantido por alguma ferramenta. Estou tentando com o ESLint, mas ainda não consegui fazer exatamente esse padrão funcionar.

items.title: Re: [討論] 台男是全世界最命苦？
items.human_voice:
其實最優解就是男生向下兼容，或者是不參與賽局，走向米格道，放下我執即是解脫，何苦

婚姻是一份長期契約。男性承諾數十年經濟供養與保護，換取排他性性接觸與血緣確定性。文化利用男性性驅力促成直接財富轉移至育兒女性，成本低於政府稅收。

婚姻並非單純的感情昇華，而是一份經過文化系統設計的長期期貨契約。男性承諾在未來數十年中持續輸出經濟供養與安全保護，以換取女性排他性的性接觸權以及確定撫養自身基因後代的權利。

透過婚姻契約自願促成直接財富轉移是成本最低且最自然的機制。現代離婚法律中強制執行的贍養費與子女撫養費制度，本質上即是文化與法律系統為確保這條財富轉移鏈條不致斷裂而設立的兜底機制。

事實上，僅需少數男性負責播種，其餘過剩的男性人口則被投入高危勞動與戰向消耗中，被當作可替換的社會耗材。

在生物繁衍的邏輯下，「精子是廉價的，卵子是昂貴的」。一個社會如果損失了 80% 的男性，剩餘的 20% 男性依然能使所有女性懷孕並維持人口規模；但若損失了 80% 的女性，該社會的人口將面臨毀滅性崩潰 。

因此，人類演化出一套將男性視為「可拋棄消耗品」的生存策略。系統透過賦予榮譽、男子氣概的稱號與微弱的特權，激勵男性去承擔高死亡率的戰爭、高污染高危險的基建勞作（如採礦、高空建築、消防），以保護女性與幼童。男性的犧牲被文化包裝為一種高尚的義務 。

然而，現代平權運動在剝離男性傳統權威與特權的同時，卻依然保留了社會對男性承擔沉重義務的期待。當代文化依然期待男性在危急時刻挺身而出、在經濟上能夠自立並為家庭兜底，但不再給予相應的尊嚴與權威。這種「義務並未減少、地位已被消解」的結構性失衡，使供養者角色從一份榮耀轉變為純粹的經濟負擔。

隨著女性大舉進入白領職場並實現經濟自立，女性不再需要依賴男性的薪水才能生存。這導致男性單純作為「經濟糧票」的邊際價值急劇下降。

當現代社會持續傳遞「男人可有可無」的訊號，同時又要求男性繼續承擔高危勞動時，男性的理性應對便是進行自發性的退縮：選擇晚婚、放棄爭取卓越、降低物質慾望並退出傳統的婚姻博弈（即「躺平」或「草食化」現象）。

As far as I know, hundreds of people were laid off in the past two years. We were told that there are no (immediate) plans for further layoffs. However, we were also told that the budget of our directorate stays the same for the next two years, so either there won't be a pay rise (even though there's some inflation that might justify it) or some people will be laid off to get funds for other people's pay rise.

Also in the past few months the behaviour of the management seems less friendly (I wouldn't say outright hostile, it's not that bad). Home office rules were tightened, working computer surveillance is introduced, more time reporting is required, etc. Management says they want to get increased productivity out of this, but sometimes I feel like they are trying to make the environment uncomfortable enough for people to leave on their own as it's cheaper than firing them. I actually did look around, but the job market is fairly bad right now :-(

By the way, in the same period the company stock price quadrupled(!). I understand that shareholders might like the layoffs (less money is spent by the company), but this price increase seems to indicate that the company is healthy and in no dire need of layoffs.
Do companies really try to nudge employees to leave?

items.title: When should I disclose an upcoming vacation that overlaps with the start date of an internal job position?
items.human_voice:
I’m interviewing for an internal position. The job posting didn’t state a start date, but I recently found out about the start date after applying. This date overlaps with the last week of my international trip for vacation (that I booked a long time prior to my application). At my current job, I have a scheduled summer break. During the summer break period, I don’t have any work and I can go on any vacation, so there’s no need to ask for approval, and my work doesn't know about this vacation.

The first week of the new job involves trainings and meetings, which I could participate remotely while abroad, but the manager needs to ask for permission from my work to allow remote work abroad. I would need to miss 1 or 2 in-person staff meetings.

items.title: How do I know when babies can go over bed guards?
items.human_voice:
My twin babies (9.5 months old) sleep in my bed. I have placed a mesh bed guard (this type) on all four sides, screwed into the bed frame.

Two nights ago, they discovered a new game: climbing up the guards. They grab the upper edge and use a combination of pull-ups and bracing their feet against the mesh to go up. They can now go at least as far up as to bite the edge from above (I see the spit marks), and the feet come up almost 20 cm above the mattress.

On the one hand, I want to think that they are still safe. They don't the upper body strength to do a very high pull up, and bracing the legs becomes more difficult the higher the legs are. I don't think I could climb over a scaled-up guard myself (although maybe I can? I don't have the opportunity to test). And the official wisdom is that these guards are safe until they reach to the baby's armpits (currently, the babies are 72-ish cm tall and the rails are 67).

On the other hand, I still feel quite worried when I see them go that high after only two evenings of exercising. They are very advanced in motor development. Also, they are underweight (around 7.5 kg), which seems to help them in any activity where their muscles have to carry their weight.

How do I recognize when they are advanced enough to be able to climb over the guard?
